Pick it up at any state park or CPW office with a DD214, military ID, a Colorado license or ID with VETERAN on it, or a VA medical card. The pass covers only the service member, is not valid at State Wildlife Areas, and camping and other fees still apply.
benefits.source_title: CPW offers free entry into Colorado state parks in August (July 31, 2025)

benefits.benefit: In-state tuition for honorably discharged veterans
benefits.details: Every Colorado public college and university must charge in-state tuition to an honorably discharged veteran who lives in Colorado, no matter how recently they moved here (no one-year wait). Schools may extend this to the veteran's dependents, but that part is optional. Students classified this way also get the College Opportunity Fund stipend. Apply through your school's registrar or veterans office with your DD-214.
benefits.source_title: C.R.S. 23-7.4-203 Tuition classification of armed forces veterans (Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 23)

benefits.benefit: Colorado National Guard tuition waiver (current Guard members)
benefits.details: Current drilling members of the Colorado Army or Air National Guard can have up to 100% of in-state tuition waived at approved Colorado public colleges after other aid is applied (HB26-1386 took effect July 1, 2026). It does not cover fees or books and is capped by credit hours (65 associate, 130 bachelor's, 145 combined). You must complete the FAFSA or CASFA and apply through DMVA's portal every semester during short windows: June 1 to 20 (fall), November 1 to 20 (spring), April 1 to 20 (summer). This is for serving Guard members, not separated veterans.
benefits.source_title: Tuition Waiver Program, Colorado DMVA

benefits.benefit: Free tuition and room and board for dependents of Guard members killed or permanently disabled on duty
benefits.details: A dependent of a Colorado National Guard member who died or was permanently disabled on state active duty, federal active duty, or authorized training can attend a Colorado state college free of tuition and room and board for a first bachelor's degree or certificate. The student must keep a 2.5 GPA and the benefit ends six years after enrollment. This is NOT a general benefit for children of 100% disabled veterans; a 2026 bill to create one (SB26-067) failed. Apply through the school's financial aid office.
benefits.source_title: C.R.S. 23-3.3-205 (Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 23)

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay income tax subtraction
benefits.details: Military retirees under age 55 at year end can subtract up to $15,000 of military retirement pay from Colorado taxable income each year from 2022 through 2028. Retirees 55 and older use the general pension and annuity subtraction instead: up to $20,000 (ages 55 to 64) or $24,000 (65+). Claim it on the Subtractions from Income Schedule (DR 0104AD). VA disability compensation is not part of federal taxable income, so Colorado does not tax it either. No cap changes took effect for 2026.
benefits.source_title: Retired Servicemembers, Colorado Department of Revenue (Income Tax Topics: Military Servicemembers, rev. Feb 2025)

benefits.benefit: Veterans' preference in state and local government hiring
benefits.details: When the State of Colorado (or a county, city, or district with a comparable merit system) scores job applicants, 10 points are added for a veteran receiving VA disability compensation or disability retired pay for a line-of-duty disability, and 5 points for an honorably separated wartime or campaign-badge veteran. Surviving spouses get 5 points; the maximum is 10, and no preference applies to promotions. Veterans also get retention preference in layoffs. Attach your DD-214 (Member 4) and, for the 10 points, a VA letter showing a service-connected disability.
benefits.source_title: Veterans' Preference, State of Colorado Careers (Colo. Const. Art. XII Sec. 15)

benefits.benefit: Colorado Veterans Community Living Centers (state veterans homes)
benefits.details: Colorado runs five state veterans homes (Aurora/Fitzsimons, Florence, Homelake near Monte Vista, Rifle, and Walsenburg) offering long-term skilled nursing, short-term rehab, memory care, respite, and hospice. Honorably discharged veterans, their spouses or widows, and Gold Star parents are eligible if they meet medical criteria; no VA rating is required. Veterans pay a lower daily rate because VA pays part of the cost. The homes accept Medicaid, Medicare (short-term rehab), and private pay. Contact the admissions office of the center you want.
benefits.source_title: Veterans Community Living Centers, Colorado Department of Human Services

states.name: Connecticut
notes: Connecticut has no county governments. Every property tax exemption is applied by your town or city assessor, and the dollar amounts differ from town to town because state law (CGS 12-62g) makes towns raise the amounts after big revaluations. Always ask your own assessor for the local figure.

The full property tax exemption on your home (CGS 12-81(83)) is only for veterans the VA has found permanently and totally disabled based on a 100% service-connected rating. A 100% schedular rating that is not P&T, and TDIU, do NOT qualify for it. TDIU veterans get the full exemption only if their town has voted to adopt the optional TDIU exemption created in 2025 (PA 25-168 sec. 240).

The 100% P&T exemption now needs an application EVERY YEAR, due to the assessor by January 1 after the October 1 assessment date, on the OPM form, with your VA letter and a signed statement that you are not claiming it in another town. If the VA drops your P&T status you lose it and fall back to the smaller 12-81(20) exemption.

The full exemption covers only the part of the home you live in. Rental units and business space in the building are taxed. If you do not own a home it shifts to one motor vehicle garaged in Connecticut. Towns may limit it to two acres or cap it at the town's median home value.

For the basic and disabled-veteran exemptions, your DD-214 must be on file with the town clerk before October 1. The income-based additional exemption (Form M-59a) is filed every two years between February 1 and October 1. Missing the date usually pushes you to the next grand list.

Surviving spouses keep most veteran exemptions only while they stay unmarried and live in Connecticut. For the 100% P&T exemption, a spouse of a veteran who died before October 1, 2024 is covered only if the town votes to include pre-2024 deaths.

Free vehicle registration (up to three vehicles) and no-fee disabled veteran plates are NOT based on a percentage rating. You must have wartime service AND a VA-certified service-connected loss or loss of use of an arm or leg, blindness, paraplegia, hemiplegia, or traumatic brain injury. The plate allows 24-hour overtime parking but does not allow use of accessible (handicapped) spaces.

There is no Connecticut free hunting or fishing license based on a VA disability percentage. The free lifetime license is for loss of a limb or loss of use of a limb (any resident), and blind residents. Residents 65 and older fish free.

The state college tuition waiver is based on 90 days of wartime service and Connecticut domicile, not on a disability rating. It waives tuition only, not fees, books, or housing, and it only applies after other federal education benefits are counted. Dependents qualify only if the parent is MIA/POW (after 1960) or was killed in action on or after 9/11/2001.

Military retirement pay is 100% exempt from Connecticut income tax (since tax year 2015) and VA disability compensation is never taxed because Connecticut starts from federal AGI. Former spouses receiving a share of retired pay under a divorce decree cannot take the exemption.

State hiring preference under CGS 5-224 is 5 points for wartime veterans and 10 points if you are eligible for VA disability compensation or pension, but it only applies to scored examinations for original appointment. The DAS website does not explain how points are applied in today's mostly exam-free hiring, so ask DAS before relying on it.

Commonly claimed but not found on any official source: a rating-based hunting/fishing license waiver, a disabled veteran exemption from the $8-per-year Passport to the Parks registration surcharge (DEEP says there are no exemptions), and a free state park camping benefit for disabled veterans (the Disabled Veteran Pass is not valid for camping).

benefits.benefit: Basic wartime veteran property tax exemption
benefits.details: Takes at least $1,000 off the assessed value of your home or vehicle (at least $1,500 once the mandatory income-based add-on in CGS 12-81g is counted; more in towns that have revalued). You must be a Connecticut resident who served 90 or more days in a period of war (or was retired after 30 years). File your DD-214 with the town clerk before the October 1 assessment date; the assessor applies it each year after that. An unmarried surviving spouse or minor child residing in Connecticut gets $1,000 ($3,000 if the death was in service).
benefits.source_title: CGS 12-81(19) and (22), Chapter 203 Property Tax Assessment

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran property tax exemption (10% or higher)
benefits.details: Reduces assessed value by $2,000 for a VA rating of 10%-25%, $2,500 for 26%-50%, $3,000 for 51%-75%, and $3,500 for 76% or higher or for any rated veteran age 65 or older (towns that have revalued apply higher amounts). Wartime service is not required; you must be a Connecticut resident. Submit your VA rating letter to the town assessor; proof is not needed again unless your rating changes, and refunds can go back up to three years if proof was late. An unmarried surviving spouse or minor children living in Connecticut keep the same amount.
benefits.source_title: CGS 12-81(20), as amended by PA 25-168 sec. 234

benefits.benefit: Severe service-connected disability home exemption ($10,000 / $5,000)
benefits.details: An extra $10,000 off the assessed value of your owner-occupied home (and lot) if the VA has found a service-connected loss of use or paralysis of both legs, hemiplegia, total blindness, or amputation of both arms, legs, hands, or feet (or a hand and a foot); $5,000 for loss of use of one arm or one leg. It is added on top of the 12-81(20) amount and applies only to your domicile. Apply through the town assessor after qualifying under 12-81(20). A surviving spouse keeps it while unmarried and living in the home. Towns may also fully exempt a home bought or adapted with VA Specially Adapted Housing funds.
benefits.source_title: CGS 12-81(21), Chapter 203 Property Tax Assessment

benefits.benefit: Full property tax exemption for 100% permanent and total (primary residence or one vehicle)
benefits.details: Your primary residence (house, condo, common-interest unit, or mobile home, including the part you occupy if some is rented or used for business) is fully exempt from property tax if you are a Connecticut resident the VA has determined to be permanently and totally disabled based on a 100% service-connected rating. If you own no home, one motor vehicle garaged in Connecticut is exempt instead. Effective October 1, 2024 (PA 24-46); since the 2025 grand list you must apply every year to the assessor by January 1 on the OPM form with your VA determination and a statement you are not claiming it in another town. An unmarried surviving spouse or minor children living in Connecticut keep it. Towns may limit the lot to two acres, cap the exemption at the town median assessed home value, or extend it to spouses of veterans who died before October 1, 2024.
benefits.source_title: CGS 12-81(83) as amended by PA 25-2 and PA 25-168 secs. 233-239 (House Bill 7287)

benefits.benefit: Municipal-option full property tax exemption for TDIU
benefits.details: Towns may vote to give veterans the VA has found to have a service-connected total disability based on individual unemployability (TDIU) the same full exemption on a primary residence (or one vehicle if no home) that 100% P&T veterans get, in place of the 12-81(20) exemption. Effective October 1, 2025. Check whether your town adopted it; if it has not, a TDIU veteran gets only the rating-based exemption. Apply to the assessor with your VA determination; spouse and unmarried surviving spouse rules mirror the P&T exemption.
benefits.source_title: PA 25-168 sec. 240 (new section, effective October 1, 2025)

benefits.benefit: Additional state veterans exemption (income-tested, up to 200%)
benefits.details: If you already get a 12-81(19), (20), (21) or (22) exemption and your income is at or below the OPM limit, the state doubles your exemption (three times, at town option, for 100%-rated veterans); veterans over the limit get a 50% add-on. For 2025 income the OPM schedule is $46,300 unmarried and $56,500 married; for 100%-rated veterans the statutory limit is $18,000 unmarried / $21,000 married ($21,000 / $24,000 under the local 3x option). VA disability payments do not count as income. File Form M-59a with the town assessor between February 1 and October 1, then every two years.
benefits.source_title: OPM Additional Veterans Tax Relief Program; CGS 12-81g; OPM 2026 Homeowners Q&A Booklet (income schedule)

benefits.benefit: Local-option veteran property tax exemptions
benefits.details: Towns may add exemptions on top of the state ones: up to $20,000 or 10% of assessed value for income-qualified wartime veterans and surviving spouses (CGS 12-81f); at least $3,000 for income-qualified rated veterans (12-81f(b)); up to $5,000 or 5% for veterans who do not qualify for the state exemptions (12-81jj); 10% of a primary residence for veterans with federal AGI of $50,100 or less (12-81kk); and a percentage exemption for one specially equipped vehicle (12-81h). Each town sets its own income limit (not below the OPM limit) and application form; most are filed with the assessor by October 1 and every two years after.
benefits.source_title: OLR Report 2023-R-0175, Veterans' Property Tax Exemptions (Oct. 6, 2023); CGS 12-81f, 12-81h, 12-81jj, 12-81kk

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran plates, free registration for 3 vehicles, overtime parking
benefits.details: No registration fee for up to three passenger, camper, or combination vehicles per year, no-charge Disabled Veteran plates, and a card allowing overtime parking up to 24 hours (not accessible spaces). You must be a Connecticut resident with wartime service AND a VA-certified service-connected amputation or loss of use of an arm or leg, blindness, paraplegia, hemiplegia, or traumatic brain injury; percentage rating alone does not qualify. Bring a VA letter on letterhead to DMV (DMV guidance says initial issuance is in person at Wethersfield); title, lien, and clean-air fees still apply. A surviving spouse keeps the plates free for life or until remarriage.
benefits.source_title: CGS 14-254 Parking privileges of disabled veterans; CGS 14-49(o); DMV Disabled Veteran Registration (class code 14) guidance

benefits.benefit: DEEP Disabled Veteran Pass (lifetime) and Passport to the Parks
benefits.details: Connecticut residents with any VA service-connected disability get a free lifetime Disabled Veteran Pass admitting the holder to Gillette Castle, Dinosaur, and Fort Trumbull State Parks; it is not valid for camping or special events. Apply in person at a DEEP or park office or by mail to DEEP State Parks Division, 79 Elm Street, Hartford, with proof of residency and a VA card or benefits letter. Separately, anyone in a Connecticut-registered vehicle parks free at all state parks and forests year-round under Passport to the Parks (funded by an $8-per-year registration surcharge with no exemptions).
benefits.source_title: DEEP Special Passes - CT State Parks and Forests (updated June 2024); DEEP Passport to the Parks (updated May 2024)

benefits.benefit: Free lifetime hunting/fishing license (loss of limb or blindness, not rating-based)
benefits.details: Connecticut has no hunting or fishing license waiver tied to a VA percentage. Any resident who has lost a limb or permanently lost the use of a limb gets a free lifetime hunting, sport fishing, or trapping license (permits and stamps still cost) with a physician, PA, or APRN certification, issued at select DEEP offices and participating town clerks. Blind residents get a free lifetime fishing license, with the VA supplying proof for veterans. Residents 65 and older get free annual fishing licenses.
benefits.source_title: CGS 26-29b and 26-29, Chapter 490 Fisheries and Game; DEEP 2026 Hunting Guide, Hunting Opportunities for Persons with Disabilities

benefits.benefit: Tuition waiver at UConn, state universities, community colleges, Charter Oak
benefits.details: Tuition is waived for undergraduate and graduate study at UConn, the four Connecticut State Universities, and CT State Community College for veterans with 90 or more cumulative days of service in a period of war (or less if separated for a service-connected disability), discharged honorably or under honorable conditions, accepted for admission, and domiciled in Connecticut at acceptance. Fees, books, and housing are not waived, and the waiver pays only what federal GI Bill benefits do not. Since July 1, 2025 (PA 25-95) extension, summer, and intersession fees are also waived and Charter Oak State College must waive tuition fees. Dependent children of service members declared MIA or POW after January 1, 1960 who are state residents also qualify. Apply through the campus veterans office when enrolling.
benefits.source_title: CGS 10a-77(d), 10a-99(d), 10a-105(e); CSCU Veterans Tuition Waiver page; PA 25-95 secs. 9-13

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay 100% exempt; VA compensation not taxed
benefits.details: Connecticut has an income tax, but retired members of the U.S. armed forces or National Guard subtract 100% of military retirement pay (Form CT-1040 Schedule 1, Line 44); surviving beneficiaries of the retiree's survivor election can take the same subtraction, while a former spouse paid under a divorce decree cannot. The full exemption has applied since tax year 2015. VA disability compensation is excluded from federal AGI and therefore is not taxed by Connecticut. No application is needed beyond the tax return.
benefits.source_title: DRS 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions, Line 44 Military Retirement Pay (Rev. 12/25); CGS 12-701(a)(20)(B)(xvi)

benefits.benefit: State civil service examination points (5 or 10)
benefits.details: On a scored state examination for original appointment, wartime veterans who pass get 5 points added; veterans eligible for VA disability compensation or pension get 10 points, as do spouses who cannot work because of the veteran's disability and unmarried surviving spouses. Veterans with a campaign badge or expeditionary medal, and service members in the last year of an enlistment, get 5 points. Claim veteran status when applying through the DAS online job system and supply your DD-214 and VA letter. DAS now fills most jobs without written exams, so ask DAS how the points apply to a given posting.
benefits.source_title: CGS 5-224 Credit for military service on examinations held for original appointments; DAS Military Talent page

benefits.benefit: Connecticut Veterans Wartime Service Medal
benefits.details: A state medal for veterans with 90 days of active wartime service (or the full length of a shorter war or operation), discharged honorably or under honorable conditions or for injuries in the line of duty, who live in Connecticut now or lived here at the time of the qualifying service. Submit CTDVA Form VM1 with your DD-214 to the Department of Veterans Affairs, 287 West Street, Rocky Hill, CT 06067 (Form VM2 for a posthumous award to family). No deadline.
benefits.source_title: CTDVA Connecticut Wartime Service Medal (page dated May 31, 2024)

benefits.benefit: Free bus passes for veterans; Rocky Hill Veterans Home
benefits.details: The Department of Veterans Affairs provides local transit bus passes to Connecticut veterans at no cost; apply online through the DVA forms site and verify status with a VA Health ID card or a Connecticut license or ID showing the veteran flag (passes are mailed monthly and are not transferable; a 2026 law makes the program permanent and adds up to 50% fare discounts on state buses). The DVA campus in Rocky Hill also runs a supportive Residential Facility and the Sgt. John L. Levitow Veterans Health Center (skilled nursing) for veterans discharged honorably or under honorable conditions who live in Connecticut now or lived here when they enlisted; apply to the DVA admissions office, 860-616-3708.
benefits.source_title: CTDVA Bus Passes for Veterans (page dated Aug. 24, 2026); CTDVA Residential Services; PA 26-21 sec. 8

states.name: Delaware

agency.name: Delaware Commission of Veterans Affairs / Office of Veterans Services (Delaware Department of State)

notes: The big Delaware property tax break is a credit against SCHOOL taxes, not county taxes. The state law requires VA compensation at the 100% rate for a permanent and total disability, 'based on individual unemployability or a 100% disability rating.' TDIU counts. A 100% rating that is not marked permanent and total may be questioned, so bring your VA letter showing P&T status.

You must have been legally domiciled in Delaware for 3 full years in a row before you can get the school tax credit. A vacation home does not count, and being gone from Delaware for 12 months is treated as giving up your domicile.

The school tax credit application is due April 30 for the coming tax year, and you must have paid the prior year's property tax bill in full. Apply through your county (New Castle 302-395-5520, Kent 302-744-2401, Sussex 302-855-7871), not the state.

County property tax relief is different in each county. Sussex and New Castle tie a county credit to the state 100% P&T / TDIU standard. Kent County's program is a general disability and senior exemption with income limits, with only the residency rules waived for 100% service-connected veterans.

A surviving spouse keeps the school tax credit only if the veteran was already getting it, the spouse was already on the deed before the death, the spouse has not remarried, and the home is still the spouse's main residence.

A bill to lower the school tax credit threshold from 100% to 80% (HB 349) was introduced in April 2026 and was still sitting in the House Appropriations Committee as of our check. It is NOT law. Do not expect an 80% rating to qualify.

Delaware does NOT have a free hunting or fishing license for all disabled veterans. The free hunt, trap and fish exemption needs an honorable discharge and a VA service-connected rating of at least 60%.

There is no free state park pass for disabled veterans in Delaware law or on the State Parks website. Any honorably discharged veteran who lives in Delaware can buy the annual pass at half price ($25) for a Delaware-registered vehicle. A disabled resident who holds a federal Gold Access Passport card is exempt from park entrance fees.

The Disabled Veteran (DAV) plate costs a one-time $10 fee and does NOT let you park in handicapped spaces. For parking privileges you need the DAV-HP plate, which also requires a doctor's certification of a walking or similar disability under 21 Del. C. § 2134.

Only one vehicle per veteran is exempt from registration fees, and only if the VA has found you eligible for the automobile or adaptive equipment grant. A rating alone does not waive the registration fee.

Delaware has no tuition waiver for disabled veterans or for their children. The state education benefit covers children (ages 16-24) of service members who died from service causes, were POWs, or are MIA, and it requires 3 years of Delaware residency.

The military pension exclusion is $12,500 regardless of age for tax year 2025 and 2026 returns. Under a law signed August 17, 2026 (SB 219) it rises to $15,000 in 2027, $20,000 in 2028 and $25,000 in 2029. Those higher amounts do not apply yet.

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veterans School Property Tax Credit
benefits.details: A credit for 100% of the non-vocational school district property tax on your primary residence. You must receive VA compensation for a service-connected permanent and total disability at the 100% rate, 'based on individual unemployability or a 100% disability rating,' and have been legally domiciled in Delaware for at least 3 consecutive years. Apply through your county assessment or billing office by April 30 before the tax year starts, with your VA letter, Delaware ID and Social Security card; you cannot also take the Senior School Property Tax Credit. A surviving spouse who was on the deed, has not remarried and still lives in the home keeps the credit.
benefits.source_title: Delaware Department of Finance - Disabled Veterans School Property Tax Credit; 14 Del. C. § 1917(d)

benefits.benefit: New Castle County disabled veteran county property tax exemption
benefits.details: New Castle County reduces the county property tax (and crossing guard tax) on a principal residence to zero for veterans who receive VA compensation for a service-connected permanent and total disability based on individual unemployability or a 100% rating, with no residency waiting period. Apply to the New Castle County Assessment Division (302-395-5520, assessment@newcastlede.gov) using the county Disability Exemption form; the 2026 form listed a June 1, 2026 filing deadline. County pages blocked our automated reader, so confirm current amounts, income rules and the deadline with the county.
benefits.source_title: New Castle County Assessment Division - Tax Exemptions (Disability Exemption Application, revised Jan. 6, 2026)

benefits.benefit: Kent County disability property tax exemption (veteran residency waiver)
benefits.details: Kent County offers a reduction in taxable assessment to owners who are 'entirely disabled (100%) with documented proof.' The program carries income limits (single AGI not over $18,000; applicant and spouse not over $24,750, excluding Social Security and disability income) and the county page does not say veterans are exempt from those limits. The 5-year Delaware residency and 1-year primary-residence rules are waived for veterans 100% disabled due to military service. File with the Kent County Assessment Office by April 30 before the tax year, with all county taxes paid, and reapply every year.
benefits.source_title: Kent County Levy Court - Tax Credits & Exemptions (Assessment)

benefits.benefit: Sussex County Real Property Tax Credit for Disabled Veterans
benefits.details: Sussex County grants a credit against its county value-based property tax to residents who qualify for the state Disabled Veterans School Tax Credit (100% P&T or TDIU, 3 years as a full-time Delaware resident as of July 1). The county says the combined credit can be 'up to a full credit towards property taxes, excluding Sussex Tech and non-value-based fees and services.' The state school tax credit application doubles as the county application; file with the Sussex County Billing Office (302-855-7871) by April 30, with all county taxes and fees paid. The credit continues for a surviving spouse who keeps owning and living in the home, but it does not transfer when the property is sold.
benefits.source_title: Sussex County - Disabled Veterans School Tax Credit; Sussex County Ordinance No. 2811 (Nov. 16, 2021)

benefits.benefit: Vehicle registration fee exemption for disabled veterans
benefits.details: One vehicle owned by a veteran with a disability who is or ever was eligible for VA automobile or adaptive equipment benefits (38 U.S.C. § 1901 et seq. or Public Law 93-538) is exempt from Delaware registration fees, limited to one automobile per veteran at a time, and the plates are furnished at no cost. This is tied to VA adaptive equipment eligibility, not to a percentage rating. Bring VA documentation of that eligibility to any DMV office; the vehicle still must pass inspection.
benefits.source_title: Delaware DMV - Military Services; 21 Del. C. § 2164

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran (DAV) and DAV-HP license plates
benefits.details: A veteran certified by the VA as having a service-connected disability, or certified by DoD as having sustained a disabling injury in a war or conflict, may get a Disabled Veteran plate for a private passenger vehicle or truck up to 26,000 lb GVWR for a one-time $10 fee plus the normal annual registration fee. The standard DAV plate 'does not permit special parking in handicapped zones.' The DAV-HP plate adds disability parking privileges but requires a physician certification of a permanent mobility, lung or cardiac condition under 21 Del. C. § 2134. Apply with Form MV549 and your VA letter at any DMV office.
benefits.source_title: Delaware DMV Form MV549 DAV License Plate Application (Rev. 4/2025); 21 Del. C. § 2138

benefits.benefit: Free hunting, trapping and fishing license exemption
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans certified by the VA as having 'at least a 60% service-connected disability' may be issued a license exemption to hunt, trap and fish in Delaware without charge. The statute does not require Delaware residency. Submit the Veterans with Disabilities Exempt Application with your VA letter directly to the DNREC Division of Fish and Wildlife and allow up to 4 weeks. Separately, any resident who served 90+ days on active duty can get a free hunting and/or fishing license during the first 12 months after discharge.
benefits.source_title: DNREC Division of Fish and Wildlife - License Exemptions; 7 Del. C. § 502(h)

benefits.benefit: Delaware State Parks Military Pass (50% off annual pass)
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans, active-duty members and military retirees who are permanent Delaware residents can buy the annual state park pass for $25 instead of $50 for each vehicle registered in Delaware in their name; passes are sold only at park offices with your DD-214, Delaware license and registration. There is no free pass based on a disability rating. Disabled Delaware residents who hold a federal Gold Access Passport card are exempt from entrance fees, and residents who served 90+ consecutive days in OIF/OEF can get a free pass for 12 months after discharge from the Dover Office of Business Services.
benefits.source_title: Delaware State Parks - Passes and Permits; 7 Del. C. § 4701(a)(5)

benefits.benefit: Educational Benefits for Children of Deceased Veterans and Others
benefits.details: Pays tuition and mandatory fees for up to 4 years, first at a Delaware public college, for a child of a service member who was killed on active duty or died of service-related causes, is a prisoner of war, or is officially missing in action. The child must be 16 to 24 years old, a Delaware resident for at least 3 consecutive years, and the parent must have been a Delaware resident at the time of death or POW/MIA status. Apply through the Delaware Higher Education Office financial aid portal; the application opens in December and closes in mid-May each year. Delaware has no tuition waiver for disabled veterans themselves or for children of living disabled veterans.
benefits.source_title: 14 Del. C. Chapter 34, Subchapter VI - Educational Benefits for Children of Deceased Veterans and Others

benefits.benefit: Military pension exclusion from state income tax
benefits.details: Delaware taxes income but lets a military retiree exclude up to $12,500 of U.S. military pension at any age (other retirees under 60 get only $2,000; everyone 60 or over gets up to $12,500 of pension and eligible retirement income). SB 219, signed August 17, 2026, phases the military amount up to $15,000 for 2027, $20,000 for 2028 and $25,000 for 2029 and later, regardless of age, with a 3-year (5-year for new residents after 2026) Delaware domicile rule for the 60-and-over exclusion. Claim it on Line 6 of Form PIT-RES and check the military pension box.
benefits.source_title: 30 Del. C. § 1106(b)(3) as amended by 85 Del. Laws c. 426 (SB 219); 2025 Form PIT-RES Instructions, Line 6 Pension Exclusion

benefits.benefit: VA disability compensation not taxed
benefits.details: Delaware taxable income starts from federal adjusted gross income, and VA disability compensation, DIC and VA pension are excluded from federal gross income, so they are not taxed by Delaware. The Delaware Division of Revenue does not publish a page that says this in plain words; the PIT-RES instructions only address military pay and the pension exclusion. Nothing to apply for; simply do not report VA compensation as income.
benefits.source_title: Delaware 2025 Form PIT-RES Instructions; 30 Del. C. § 1105-1106 (Delaware AGI based on federal AGI)

benefits.benefit: State Merit employment preference points
benefits.details: Veterans who meet the job's minimum qualifications get preference points added to their ranking score for state Merit System jobs: up to 10 points for disabled veterans and 5 points for other honorably discharged veterans or Delaware Guard/Reserve members with 20+ years. Five points go to the unremarried surviving spouse of a veteran, the spouse of a service member missing or captured over 90 days, or the spouse of a veteran with a service-connected disability. Preference applies only to original entrance, not promotions or layoffs. Send your DD-214 and VA disability letter to the Department of Human Resources by 4:30 p.m. the business day after the posting closes.
benefits.source_title: Delaware Employment Link - Veterans' Preference; 29 Del. C. § 5935

benefits.benefit: Delaware Veterans Home (Milford)
benefits.details: A 150-bed state long-term care facility with skilled nursing and a dementia unit at 100 Delaware Veterans Blvd., Milford. Applicants must have been honorably discharged with at least 180 days of active service (or Guard/Reserve equivalents, or be a Gold Star family member), have lived in Delaware for at least one year before applying, and have a medically determined need for long-term care. Apply with the admissions packet to DOSDVH_Admissions@delaware.gov or call 302-424-6000.
benefits.source_title: Delaware Veterans Home - Application for Admission

benefits.benefit: Delaware Veterans Trust Fund emergency assistance
benefits.details: One-time financial help for Delaware resident veterans with an honorable or general-under-honorable-conditions discharge who have a documented emergency need (rent or mortgage, utilities, medical bills, car payments and similar). Funds are paid directly to the vendor, approval is not guaranteed, and the fund depends on donations. Submit the application with DD-214, Delaware ID, bills, two recent pay stubs and two bank statements to DOS_OVS@delaware.gov or at the Bear, Dover or Millsboro veterans offices.
benefits.source_title: Delaware Office of Veterans Services - Veterans Trust Fund

benefits.benefit: Paraplegic Veterans Pension ($3,000 per year)
benefits.details: Delaware pays a state pension of $3,000 per year in equal monthly installments to veterans who are paraplegic and fully disabled due to service during a period of war. This is a unique Delaware benefit listed on the Office of Veterans Services benefits page; contact the Office of Veterans Services (800-344-9900) to apply. We could not locate the application form or the statute section online, so confirm documentation requirements with the office.
benefits.source_title: Delaware Office of Veterans Services - Veterans Benefits

states.name: District of Columbia
notes: The $445,000 property tax deduction needs a VA rating that is 'total and permanent' OR payment at the 100% rate for unemployability (TDIU). A plain 100% schedular rating that is not marked permanent does not match the law's words.
The $445,000 deduction has an income cap. For tax year 2026, total household federal adjusted gross income for 2024 must be under $163,500. The cap changes every year.

You apply for the veterans deduction with the Mayor's Office of Veterans Affairs online, not with the tax office. File between October 1 and March 31 to get the whole year. File April 1 to September 30 and you only get half, on the second bill.
You cannot stack the veterans deduction with the regular Homestead Deduction, the 50% Senior/Disabled Tax Relief, or the assessment cap credit. It replaces them.

Surviving spouses and domestic partners can keep or claim the $445,000 deduction starting October 1, 2025 (D.C. Law 26-83), but only if the home was getting it when the veteran died, or would have qualified if the veteran had applied.

You must own at least 50% of the home by deed, live in it as your main home, and be domiciled in DC. Homes in an irrevocable trust (other than a special needs trust) or owned by an LLC do not qualify.
DC taxes military retirement pay in full. The old $3,000 exclusion for people 62 and older ended with tax year 2014. VA disability compensation is not taxed because it is not in federal gross income.

The DMV 'no fee' tag is for one vehicle only, only for veterans the VA calls 'Total and Permanent,' and it only waives the yearly registration fee. Specialty tag application and display fees may still apply.
A disability placard or tag in DC does not give free parking. You get double the posted time at meters, but you still pay the meter.

DC government hiring preference is 5 points for honorable service over 180 days plus 5 more for a service-connected disability, but it ends 5 years after you leave the service, and military retirees get no preference at all.
DC has no hunting, no state park pass, and no fishing license break for disabled veterans. The fishing license is $10 and only people under 16 or 65 and older are exempt.

DC has no tuition waiver for disabled veterans or their children. UDC only gives in-state tuition to GI Bill users who live in DC and enroll within 3 years of discharge, which federal law already requires.

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veterans Homestead Deduction ($445,000)
benefits.details: Takes $445,000 off the assessed value of your DC home before tax is figured. You qualify if the VA classified you as having a total and permanent service-connected disability, or you are paid at the 100% rate for unemployability, you own at least 50% of the home by deed, live there as your main home, are domiciled in DC, and household federal AGI for 2024 is under $163,500 for tax year 2026. Apply online with the Mayor's Office of Veterans Affairs; file October 1 to March 31 for the full year, or April 1 to September 30 for half. Surviving spouses and domestic partners qualify starting October 1, 2025.
benefits.source_title: DC Code § 47-850(a-2) Residential property tax relief — Homestead deduction; OTR Real Property Tax Reliefs page

benefits.benefit: Senior Citizen or Disabled Property Owner Tax Relief (50%)
benefits.details: Cuts the property tax bill by 50% for an owner who is 65 or older, or who has an SSA permanent and total disability finding, gets SSI/SSDI, railroad disability, or federal or DC government disability payments, owns at least 50% of the home, and has household federal AGI under $163,500 for tax year 2026. This is a general DC program, not a veteran program, and it cannot be combined with the $445,000 veterans deduction. Apply through OTR (MyTax.DC.gov) once eligible. OTR does not say whether VA compensation alone counts as a federal disability payment.
benefits.source_title: OTR: Real Property Tax Reliefs, Credits and Deductions; DC Code § 47-863

benefits.benefit: No-fee vehicle tags for P&T veterans
benefits.details: A veteran with a service-connected permanent and total disability can get one set of tags (DAV, Veteran, or standard passenger) at no fee for one non-commercial vehicle. Only the annual registration fee is waived. Bring a VA letter that says 'Total and Permanent' to a DC DMV service center. The statutory basis was not located in the DC Code; the DMV web page is the source.
benefits.source_title: DC DMV: Specialty Vehicle Tags

benefits.benefit: DC Veteran specialty license plates
benefits.details: Any DC-resident veteran discharged under conditions other than dishonorable, or a veteran's spouse, can get Veteran tags (branch designs) for a passenger car, pickup, or van. Cost is a $52 one-time application fee plus a $26 yearly display fee, on top of regular registration unless the P&T no-fee rule applies. Show a DD 214, WD AGO, or DD 256 at DC DMV. When the veteran dies the tags transfer to the surviving spouse for life or until remarriage.
benefits.source_title: DC Code § 50-1501.02a Issuance of veterans' license plates

benefits.benefit: Disabled American Veteran (DAV) tags
benefits.details: DAV tags are issued for a passenger vehicle at normal registration fees to a veteran certified as a member of the DC chapter of Disabled American Veterans by its Commander. You also need the VA authorization letter and an approved DC DMV disability tag/placard application, so the tag carries DC disability parking privileges (double meter time after paying). No VA percentage is stated by DMV; eligibility runs through DAV membership and the disability tag approval.
benefits.source_title: DC DMV: Specialty Vehicle Tags; DC Code § 50-1501.03(a)(3)(C)

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart license plates
benefits.details: DC residents who received the Purple Heart, or their unremarried surviving spouse, can get a Purple Heart tag for a $10 one-time application fee with no annual display fee (new law effective May 21, 2026). Prove the award with a DD-214/DD-215, WD-AGO 53-55, award orders, or an award certificate at DC DMV. Regular registration fees still apply unless the P&T no-fee rule applies.
benefits.source_title: DC Code § 50-1501.02o Purple Heart award recipient motor vehicle identification tags (D.C. Law 26-114)

benefits.benefit: Disability parking placard and parking privileges
benefits.details: DC DMV issues disability placards free and disability tags for $10 to DC residents with a qualifying mobility impairment certified by a medical practitioner (one placard and one set of tags per person). Holders may park in designated disabled spaces and for double the posted time at meters, including red top meters, after paying the meter rate. There is no free metered parking and no veteran-specific parking privilege in DC.
benefits.source_title: DC DMV: Apply for Disability Parking Placards and Permits; DDOT Parking for Persons with Disabilities

benefits.benefit: Veteran designation on driver license or ID
benefits.details: Honorably discharged veterans can have 'Veteran' printed on a DC driver license or non-driver ID card. Bring a DD 214, WD AGO, or DD 256 to a DC DMV service center. No separate fee is listed.
benefits.source_title: DC DMV: Veteran Designation

benefits.benefit: Fishing license (no disabled veteran exemption)
benefits.details: DC has no fishing license discount or exemption for disabled veterans. A resident annual license is $10 (non-resident $13), sold online by DOEE for the calendar year. Only people under 16 and people 65 and older are exempt. DC has no hunting and no state park pass program.
benefits.source_title: DOEE: Get a Fishing License

benefits.benefit: UDC in-state tuition for GI Bill users living in DC
benefits.details: The University of the District of Columbia charges the in-state rate and waives its 12-month residency wait for a veteran using Montgomery GI Bill (ch. 30) or Post-9/11 GI Bill (ch. 33) who lives in DC and enrolls within three years of discharge from active duty of 90 days or more, and for people using transferred Post-9/11 benefits on the same terms, as long as they stay continuously enrolled. Contact UDC's Office of Military and Veteran Student Services. DC has no separate tuition waiver for disabled veterans or their dependents.
benefits.source_title: UDC Policy on Student Residency Classification (Veterans section)

benefits.benefit: DC National Guard Tuition Assistance
benefits.details: DC funds a tuition assistance program for members and new recruits of the DC National Guard who are DC residents. Dollar caps, school limits, and service obligations are set by DC National Guard policy memos, which could not be retrieved. Apply through the DC National Guard education office.
benefits.source_title: DC Code § 49-807 National Guard tuition assistance benefits

benefits.benefit: DC income tax: military retirement taxed, VA compensation not taxed
benefits.details: DC has an income tax that starts from federal gross income. VA disability compensation is not in federal gross income, so DC does not tax it. Military retirement pay is fully taxable in DC; the $3,000 exclusion for retirees 62 and older applied only to tax years before January 1, 2015 and was repealed by D.C. Law 20-155. Survivor benefits from the federal or DC government are excluded for people 62 and older (D-40 Line 12), and a general disability income exclusion up to $10,000 (Form D-2440) exists for people with an SSA or government disability determination and household AGI under $100,000.
benefits.source_title: DC Code § 47-1803.02 Gross income — Items included and excluded; OTR 2025 D-40 Booklet

benefits.benefit: DC government veterans hiring preference
benefits.details: For DC government Career and Educational Service jobs, a veteran with more than 180 consecutive days of active duty and an honorable separation gets 5 extra points, and 5 more points if the veteran has a service-connected disability or receives VA compensation, disability retirement, or pension. The preference ends 5 years after separation, military retirees get none, and people who entered service after October 14, 1976 must have served in wartime. Unremarried surviving spouses and spouses of service-connected disabled veterans get the federal-equivalent preference. Claim it on the DC government job application (dchr.dc.gov). A separate 10-point preference goes to any DC resident who agrees to stay a resident 7 years.
benefits.source_title: DC Code § 1-607.03 Veterans preference in employment

benefits.benefit: VetsRide free transportation
benefits.details: Free rides through the Department of For-Hire Vehicles and the Mayor's Office of Veterans Affairs for veteran residents of DC with annual income under $45,000 or who are recently unemployed. Register or book a ride at (202) 745-5555. Monthly trip limits are not stated on the DFHV page.
benefits.source_title: DFHV: VetsRide

benefits.benefit: Veterans Navigator Office (DC Superior Court)
benefits.details: Search results show a DC Superior Court Veterans Navigator Office (Moultrie Courthouse, Room 120B, 202-879-1259) that links court-involved veterans to legal aid, housing, treatment, employment, and VA benefits help in criminal, civil, family, and landlord-tenant cases. The page now returns 'Page Not Found' after the courts' website redesign, and no formal DC Veterans Treatment Court docket could be confirmed on dccourts.gov.
benefits.source_title: DC Courts: Serving Veterans / Veterans Navigator Office (page not found at time of check) (original page moved; DC Courts home page linked)

states.name: Florida
notes: The full homestead exemption needs a VA letter that says you are 'totally and permanently disabled.' A 100% rating that is not marked permanent does not match the law's words. TDIU is not named in the statute, so ask the VA for a P&T letter and check with your county property appraiser.
You must be a Florida permanent resident on January 1 and the home must be your homestead. Only the $5,000 exemption (10% or more) can be used on property that is not your homestead.

File with the county property appraiser by March 1. You may apply before your VA letter arrives; the exemption is dated back to your application and refunds are limited to 4 years. If you miss March 1, most counties take late applications until 25 days after the August TRIM notice.

A surviving spouse keeps the exemption only while holding title, living in the home, and staying unmarried. If the spouse moves, only the dollar amount from the last tax roll moves with them. At least one county website adds a 5-year marriage rule that is not in the statute, so verify locally.
The 65-and-older discount only counts disabilities the VA identifies as combat-related, and the discount percentage equals your rating percentage. It is a reduction, not a full exemption.

The free DV plate needs a 100% rating for compensation (P&T is not required), an honorable discharge, and either 5 years of continuous Florida residency or a filed Florida domicile declaration. You get only one free plate; extra DV plates cost regular fees. Choosing a military or specialty plate instead means you pay that plate's fees. The parking-fee exemption only applies when the disabled veteran is actually in the vehicle, and event venues may still charge.
No toll exemption for DV or DV-wheelchair plates exists in Florida law. The only disability toll permit is for drivers with permanent upper-limb impairments in a specially equipped vehicle.

The free driver license or ID card is only for 100% permanent and total veterans (or holders of the FDVA ID card). The 'Veteran' license designation is for any honorably discharged veteran and does not waive the regular license fee.

Free hunting and fishing licenses start at a 50% rating (since July 1, 2024) or a VA total and permanent rating. You must apply through GoOutdoorsFlorida.com or a tax collector; the license does not cover the federal duck stamp, tarpon tags, alligator hunts, or quota hunts. The $20 Military Gold Sportsman's License is for active duty and military retirees only, not for disabled veterans who did not retire.

The free lifetime state park pass requires an honorable discharge and any service-connected disability. All other veterans get 25% off annual passes. County and city park discounts are required by law but the amount varies by county or city.

Florida has no state income tax, so military retired pay and VA compensation are never taxed by the state. Business-license fee waivers are for any honorably discharged veteran (within 60 months of discharge for state professional licenses); there is no 50% disability rule.

The children-and-spouses scholarship needs the veteran's Florida home of record in DEERS (or Florida residency), a 100% P&T rating or service-connected death, a child aged 16 to 22, and a Florida Financial Aid Application filed by April 1 for priority funding.

benefits.benefit: Total homestead property tax exemption for total and permanent service-connected disability
benefits.details: Your entire homestead is exempt from property tax if you were honorably discharged, have a service-connected total and permanent disability, hold a VA letter certifying you are totally and permanently disabled, and are a Florida permanent resident on January 1. TDIU is not named in the law; a 100% rating not marked permanent does not meet the wording. A surviving spouse keeps the exemption while holding title, living in the home and not remarrying, and may move a capped amount to a new home. File Form DR-501 with your county property appraiser by March 1; you may file before the VA letter arrives and get a refund back to the application date (4-year limit).
benefits.source_title: F.S. 196.081 Exemption for certain permanently and totally disabled veterans and for surviving spouses of veterans (2026 Florida Statutes)

benefits.benefit: $5,000 property tax exemption for 10%+ service-connected disability
benefits.details: Florida exempts $5,000 of property value for an honorably discharged ex-servicemember who is a bona fide Florida resident and is disabled 10 percent or more by misfortune or during wartime service. The Department of Revenue states it is not limited to homestead property. The unremarried surviving spouse also gets it. File Form DR-501 with your county property appraiser by March 1 with your VA rating letter; counties report it renews automatically.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 196.24 Exemption for disabled ex-servicemember or surviving spouse (2026 Florida Statutes); DOR PT-109 (R. 08/24)

benefits.benefit: Combat-related disability property tax discount for veterans age 65 and older
benefits.details: If you are 65 or older, honorably discharged, and partially or totally permanently disabled from a combat-related cause, your homestead tax is discounted by a percentage equal to your VA service-connected disability percentage (applied after other exemptions). Submit Form DR-501DV to the county property appraiser by March 1 with a VA letter stating the percentage and evidence the disability is combat-related, your DD-214, and proof of age; late filers may petition the value adjustment board. The discount carries over to a surviving spouse who holds title, lives there and does not remarry.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 196.082 Discounts for disabled veterans; surviving spouse carryover (2026 Florida Statutes)

benefits.benefit: Total homestead exemption for wheelchair-using, quadriplegic, paraplegic or legally blind veterans
benefits.details: Two separate total exemptions: (1) F.S. 196.091 exempts the homestead of an honorably discharged veteran with a service-connected total disability who received VA specially adapted housing assistance and must use a wheelchair; (2) F.S. 196.101 exempts the homestead of any quadriplegic, and of any paraplegic, hemiplegic, wheelchair-dependent or legally blind totally and permanently disabled person subject to a household income cap (statutory base $14,500, indexed yearly; VA and Social Security benefits count as income). Proof is a VA certificate or Form DR-416 from two Florida doctors, filed with the county property appraiser by March 1.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 196.101 Exemption for totally and permanently disabled persons; F.S. 196.091 Exemption for disabled veterans confined to wheelchairs (2026 Florida Statutes)

benefits.benefit: Free Disabled Veteran (DV) license plate, DV wheelchair plate, and parking-fee exemption
benefits.details: One free DV plate (or a free DV plate with the wheelchair symbol, which also carries disabled-parking-permit privileges) for an honorably discharged veteran with a VA 100% service-connected rating for compensation, a 100% rating with military disability retirement pay, or a vehicle bought with a VA auto grant, who has lived in Florida 5 continuous years or filed a Florida domicile declaration. Only the first plate is tax-free; additional DV plates pay regular fees, and since 2024 you may choose a military or specialty plate instead but must pay its fees. Vehicles with these plates are exempt from fees on public streets, metered and timed parking when the veteran is in the vehicle. Apply at a county tax collector with your VA 100% letter or FDVA ID card; renewals require a certified statement of continued eligibility.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 320.084 Free motor vehicle license plate to certain disabled veterans; F.S. 320.0842; F.S. 316.1964; FLHSMV Procedure RS-17 (Rev. 07/26)

benefits.benefit: No-fee driver license or ID card for 100% permanent and total veterans
benefits.details: An honorably discharged veteran with a VA 100-percent total and permanent service-connected rating for compensation (or an FDVA identification card, or a 100% T&P rating with military disability retirement pay) is exempt from all driver license and ID card fees under F.S. 322.21. Bring your FDVA ID card or VA letter to any FLHSMV or tax collector driver license office. Any honorably discharged veteran may also add a free 'Veteran' designation to their license by showing a DD-214 or VA ID card.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 322.21(7) License fees (2026 Florida Statutes); FLHSMV Military & Veterans Information page

benefits.benefit: No-cost Persons with Disabilities Resident Hunting and Fishing License
benefits.details: FWC issues hunting, freshwater and saltwater fishing licenses and most permits (deer, WMA, archery, muzzleloader, crossbow, turkey, Florida waterfowl, snook, lobster) at no cost to a Florida resident honorably discharged veteran with a VA service-connected rating of 50 percent or greater, or to any resident the VA certifies as totally and permanently disabled or who holds the FDVA 100% ID card. The veteran license is good for 5 years. It does not cover the federal duck stamp, tarpon tags, the statewide alligator hunt or quota hunts. Apply online at GoOutdoorsFlorida.com (FWC reviews within about 10 business days) or at a county tax collector with proof of Florida residency and your VA rating letter.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 379.353 Recreational licenses and permits; exemptions from fees and requirements; FWC Persons with Disabilities Resident Hunting/Fishing License page

benefits.benefit: Free lifetime Florida State Parks family entrance pass; 25% annual pass discount; local park discounts
benefits.details: By statute, honorably discharged veterans with a service-connected disability of any percentage receive a lifetime family annual entrance pass at no charge, and surviving spouses and parents of members who fell in combat get the same. All active duty members and honorably discharged veterans get 25 percent off annual entrance passes. Present your DD-214 and VA disability documentation; state park pages indicate passes are issued in person at a park ranger station (not verified because the parks website blocked access). Counties and cities must also offer a partial or full park entrance fee discount to veterans, but the amount varies locally.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 258.0145 Military, law enforcement, and firefighter state park fee discounts; ch. 2016-196 (s. 125.029 and s. 166.0447)

benefits.benefit: Congressman C.W. Bill Young out-of-state tuition fee waiver, transcript fee waiver, and Purple Heart tuition waiver
benefits.details: Florida public universities, state colleges and career centers must waive out-of-state fees for any honorably discharged veteran, and for anyone using VA education benefits, who physically lives in Florida while enrolled, so they pay in-state rates. The same schools waive transcript fees for veterans, active duty members and their spouses and dependents. Recipients of a Purple Heart or a higher combat decoration who are Florida residents now or were at the time of the action get undergraduate and career-certificate tuition waived for up to 110 percent of required credit hours. Apply through the school's registrar or veterans office with your DD-214.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 1009.26(8), (13), (17) Fee waivers (2026 Florida Statutes)

benefits.benefit: Disabled veteran tuition and fee gap waiver (Post-9/11 GI Bill)
benefits.details: A Florida-resident veteran rated by the VA as 100 percent total and permanent (or 100% with military disability retirement pay, or holding the FDVA ID card) who uses the Post-9/11 GI Bill at a state university, Florida College System institution, district career center or charter technical career center, but does not qualify for the federal 100-percent benefit tier, gets a waiver equal to the difference between what the GI Bill pays and the school's full tuition and fees. The waiver is applied after federal benefits; apply through the school's veterans certifying office.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 295.011 Disabled veterans; education (2026 Florida Statutes)

benefits.benefit: Scholarships for Children and Spouses of Deceased or Disabled Veterans (CSDDV)
benefits.details: Pays tuition and registration fees at a Florida public college or university (or the equivalent average at an eligible private school) for a dependent child aged 16 to 22, or the spouse, of a veteran who died from service-connected causes on active duty, is rated 100 percent permanent and total by the VA (or 100% with disability retirement pay or holds the FDVA ID card), or is a POW/MIA. Florida must have been the veteran's home of record in DEERS, or the student must be a Florida resident for tuition with the veteran living in Florida. A spouse of a disabled veteran must have been married at least 1 year; a surviving spouse must be unremarried and apply within 5 years of the death. File the Florida Financial Aid Application (opens October 1) by April 1 for priority funding; FDVA certifies the veteran.
benefits.source_title: FDOE Office of Student Financial Assistance, Scholarships for Children and Spouses of Deceased or Disabled Veterans 2026-27 Fact Sheet; F.S. 295.01-295.04

benefits.benefit: No state personal income tax (military retired pay and VA compensation untaxed)
benefits.details: Florida does not impose a personal income tax, so there are no state filing requirements and no state tax on military retired pay, VA disability compensation, DIC or SBP. The Department of Revenue cites Article VII, Section 5 of the Florida Constitution. Nothing to apply for.
benefits.source_title: Florida Department of Revenue FAQ: Do I have to file a personal income tax return in Florida?

benefits.benefit: Veterans' preference in state and local government hiring
benefits.details: Florida and its counties, cities and school districts must give hiring and retention preference. On scored selections, 20 points are added for veterans with any compensable service-connected disability and for spouses of veterans with a permanent total service-connected disability who cannot work; 15 points for wartime veterans, unremarried surviving spouses of veterans who died of service-connected causes, and parents or spouses of members killed in combat; 10 points for any other veteran or current reservist or Guard member. Veterans rated 30 percent or more go to the top of the list. For unscored positions, disabled veterans get first preference and must be interviewed if minimally qualified; agencies may waive college-degree requirements for honorably discharged veterans. Claim it on the application (People First for state jobs) with your DD-214 and VA rating letter.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 295.07 Preference in appointment and retention; F.S. 295.08; F.S. 295.085 (2026 Florida Statutes)

benefits.benefit: Professional license and local business tax fee waivers for veterans
benefits.details: The Department of Business and Professional Regulation waives the initial license, application and unlicensed-activity fees for any honorably discharged veteran or their spouse who applies within 60 months after the veteran's discharge (no disability rating required). Separately, honorably discharged veterans, their spouses and unremarried surviving spouses are exempt from county and city local business taxes and related fees, and so is a business with fewer than 100 employees that the veteran majority-owns; sign the local government's Request for Fee Exemption form with proof of discharge.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 455.213(13) General licensing provisions; F.S. 205.055 Exemptions; veterans, spouses of veterans (2026 Florida Statutes)

benefits.benefit: State Veterans' Nursing Homes and FDVA 100% P&T identification card
benefits.details: FDVA operates state veterans' nursing homes; to be admitted you must be a veteran (or a veteran's spouse or surviving spouse), need nursing home care, be a Florida resident when you apply, owe FDVA nothing from a prior stay, have applied for available financial assistance, and be approved for care by the VA. Priority goes first to Florida-resident veterans, then to those whose service-connected disability is the reason care is needed. Separately, FDVA issues an identification card to Florida permanent residents rated 100 percent service-connected permanent and total, which serves as proof for most state benefits (but not the property tax exemptions). Apply through FDVA; FDVA's web pages could not be fetched, so confirm current application packets at floridavets.org.
benefits.source_title: F.S. 296.36 Eligibility and priority of admittance; F.S. 295.17 Identification cards (2026 Florida Statutes)

states.name: Georgia
notes: The homestead exemption is not a full exemption. It removes a fixed dollar amount of value ($121,812 for 2025; DeKalb County lists $126,526 for 2026) from your home's value. Value above that is still taxed. GDVS says it 'makes no guarantees' and that each of Georgia's 159 county tax commissioners administers the rules, so proof and practice vary by county.

For the homestead exemption, GDVS lists three doors in: 'VA-rated 100 percent totally disabled,' or rated less than 100% but 'paid at the 100 percent rate due to unemployability' (TDIU), or a VA statutory award for loss of use of hands, feet, or sight. The word 'permanent' does not appear in the GDVS homestead criteria, but for the one-vehicle ad valorem exemption GDVS says '100 percent totally and permanently.' Some counties ask for a VA letter saying 100% or TDIU. Bring your VA Summary of Benefits letter.

File the homestead application with your county tax commissioner (some counties use the tax assessor). You must own and live in the home on January 1. The historic deadline is April 1, but the Department of Revenue now says you may apply up to the end of your 45-day window to appeal your notice of assessment. Missing it means waiting a year.

Surviving spouse rule for the homestead: the exemption continues for the 'unremarried surviving spouse or minor children' only 'as long as they continue to occupy the home as a residence.' Remarrying or moving ends it.

The vehicle tax break is on ONLY one vehicle, and GDVS says it is the one 'upon which the free Disabled Veteran (DV) license plate is attached.' You can get free DV plates for up to two vehicles, but only one gets the tax exemption. The plate itself is not issued for motor homes.

The free one-time veterans hunting and fishing license is for ANY honorably discharged veteran with 90+ days of active federal duty discharged on or after July 1, 2005. It is good for one year and 'may be issued only once.' After that, disabled veterans pay the low disability rate ($18 for three years) or buy a discounted lifetime license.

Georgia does NOT give disabled veterans or their children a tuition waiver at state colleges. The HERO Scholarship is for Georgia National Guard and Reserve members who deployed to a combat zone, and their children and spouses (including when the member became 100% disabled from combat injuries). It is not for regular active-duty veterans. In-state tuition for recently separated veterans comes from a Board of Regents waiver, not GDVS.

Military retirement: for tax years 2022 through 2026, only retirees under 62 get the $17,500 military exclusion (plus another $17,500 if you have more than $17,500 of Georgia earned income). Retirees 62 and older use the general retirement exclusion instead. HB 266 (signed 2025) raises the military exclusion to $65,000 for anyone under 65, but only for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2027, and you cannot stack it with the general retirement exclusion.

The 10-point state hiring preference needs a VA service-connected rating of at least 10%. The 5-point credit is for wartime veterans. Points are added to a passing score on a scored exam; if there is no exam, the agency must give 'appropriate consideration.' Preference does not apply to promotions or transfers.
The business license (occupation tax) exemption at 10% or more is handled through your county probate court, not GDVS, and lasts ten years. Counties may require extra forms.

Several property tax measures for disabled veterans (full-value exemption, partial-rating exemptions, surviving-spouse expansions) were proposed in the 2025-2026 session and may appear on the November 2026 ballot. None of them is law yet as of this review and we could not confirm their final status. Do not count on them until the Department of Revenue posts them.

Commonly believed but NOT found on an official Georgia source: that disabled veterans pay no property tax at all, that any rating under 100% qualifies for the homestead exemption, that the DV plate gives free parking statewide, and that VA disability is required to be reported on the Georgia return.

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran Homestead Tax Exemption
benefits.details: Removes a set amount of your home's value from property tax: the greater of $32,500 or the federal Specially Adapted Housing cap under 38 U.S.C. 2102 ($121,812 for 2025; DeKalb County's 2026 sheet lists $126,526). Value above that stays taxable. You qualify if you are an honorably discharged Georgia resident who owns and lives in the home and are VA-rated 100% totally disabled, OR rated less than 100% but paid at the 100% rate due to unemployability (TDIU), OR have a VA statutory award for loss or loss of use of feet, hands, or sight. The unremarried surviving spouse or minor children keep it while they live in the home. Apply with your county tax commissioner (or tax assessor); you must own and occupy the home on January 1, and file by April 1 (DOR now allows filing up to the end of your 45-day assessment appeal window).
benefits.source_title: GDVS - Disabled Veteran Homestead Tax Exemption (O.C.G.A. 48-5-48); DOR Property Tax Homestead Exemptions

benefits.benefit: Ad Valorem / Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT) Exemption on One Vehicle
benefits.details: No annual ad valorem tax or one-time title ad valorem tax (TAVT, normally 7% of value) on ONE vehicle you own. GDVS says it is for veterans 'verified by VA to be 100 percent totally and permanently service-connected disabled' and veterans rated unemployable who are entitled to certain VA statutory awards; the Department of Revenue lists 'Disabled Veterans compensated at 100%.' GDVS says the exemption applies only to the vehicle carrying the free Disabled Veteran plate. Unremarried surviving spouses and minor children are covered under O.C.G.A. 48-5-478. File Form MV-30 with your VA letter at your county tag office.
benefits.source_title: GDVS - Tax Exemptions: Ad Valorem Tax on Vehicles; DOR Form MV-30 (Rev. 06/2025)

benefits.benefit: Free Disabled Veteran License Plate (up to 2 vehicles)
benefits.details: A free Disabled Veteran plate with no registration, manufacturing, or annual fee, for up to 2 motorcycles or vehicles (not motor homes). You qualify if you are an honorably discharged Georgia veteran who is VA-rated 100% totally disabled, OR rated less than 100% but paid at the 100% rate due to unemployability, OR have a VA statutory award for loss or loss of use of feet, hands, or sight. Unremarried surviving spouses and surviving minor children also qualify. Apply through the Department of Revenue Special Tag Unit (404-968-3880) with your VA entitlement letter, or through a GDVS field office with a physician's certified statement. We could not find an official Georgia page confirming the plate's parking privileges, so do not assume it replaces a disabled parking permit.
benefits.source_title: GDVS - License Plates: Disabled Veteran; DOR Military & Veteran License Plates

benefits.benefit: Sales Tax Exemption on a VA-Grant Adapted Vehicle
benefits.details: If you receive a VA automobile grant to buy and specially adapt a vehicle for your disability, the sale of that vehicle is exempt from Georgia sales/title ad valorem tax under O.C.G.A. 48-8-3(30). The rating threshold is set by the VA grant program, not Georgia. GDVS says the exemption applies only to the original grant purchase. Bring the VA grant letter and Form MV-30 to your county tag office.
benefits.source_title: DOR Form MV-30 Georgia Veteran's Affidavit for Relief of State and Local Title Ad Valorem Tax Fees

benefits.benefit: Free Veteran Driver's License or State ID
benefits.details: Georgia residents who served and were released with any discharge other than dishonorable get a free driver's license and/or ID card marked VETERAN. Bring your DD-214 (Member 4 copy) or a GDVS Certificate of Eligibility to any Department of Driver Services (DDS) center. First-time Georgia applicants must also meet normal residency and ID requirements. National Guard members who served on active duty or have 20 years of service also qualify per GDVS.
benefits.source_title: DDS - Veterans License Process Simplified (Feb. 1, 2022); GDVS - Veteran Driver's License

benefits.benefit: One-Time Free Veterans Hunting & Fishing License
benefits.details: A free full-privilege sportsman's license, valid one year from issue, for Georgia resident veterans who served 90 or more days on active federal duty and were honorably discharged on or after July 1, 2005. It may be issued only once. Apply through Georgia DNR Wildlife Resources Division with a copy of your DD-214 and Georgia license or ID. After it expires, honorably discharged resident veterans can buy an Adult Lifetime Sportsman's License at a 20% discount (ages 16-49).
benefits.source_title: Georgia DNR WRD - One-Time Veterans Hunting & Fishing License

benefits.benefit: Resident Disability Hunting & Fishing License (3-year, $18)
benefits.details: Georgia residents who are totally and permanently disabled can buy a discounted Sportsman's Disability License for $15 plus a $3 fee for three years ($18 total), or hunting-only or fishing-only for $12 for three years. DNR's application accepts a U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs 100% disability as proof; GDVS describes it as a 'permanent and total disability rating from VA.' Hunter education is required for licenses that include hunting if you were born on or after January 1, 1961. Apply online at gooutdoorsgeorgia.com or by mail with the WRD Certification of Disability form; once approved for a permanent disability you do not have to reapply.
benefits.source_title: Georgia DNR WRD - Resident Disability Hunting & Fishing License Options

benefits.benefit: 25% State Parks Discount for Disabled Veterans
benefits.details: Georgia resident disabled veterans who present a GDVS Certificate of Eligibility card get 25% off individual accommodations (one per person), recreation fees, golf, parking, and historic site admission under O.C.G.A. 12-3-9.1. Online bookings are charged in full and refunded at check-in when you show the card. Separately, the annual ParkPass ($70; daily parking is $10) is 25% off for active military and all veterans, and 50% off for seniors 62+; discounted passes must be bought in person. We could not find an official page stating the minimum VA rating needed for the Certificate of Eligibility card.
benefits.source_title: Georgia State Parks - Reservations & Discounts; Georgia State Parks - ParkPass

benefits.benefit: Business Certificate of Exemption (Occupation Tax Waiver)
benefits.details: Veterans discharged under honorable conditions with a VA service-connected rating of 10% or more are exempt for ten years from local occupation taxes, administrative fees, and regulatory fees for peddling, running a business, or practicing a profession (O.C.G.A. 43-12-1). Complete GDVS VS Form 40-025 and take it with ID, your DD-214, and your VA Summary of Benefits letter to your county probate court; the probate judge issues a notarized certificate you then use to register with your county tax commissioner. Some counties also require VS Form 40-026. A 2025-2026 bill (HB 632) proposed clarifying eligibility; we could not confirm it became law.
benefits.source_title: GDVS - Business Certificate of Exemption

benefits.benefit: State Employment Veterans' Preference (5 or 10 points)
benefits.details: On state jobs with a numerically scored written entrance exam, honorably discharged veterans who served during a time of armed conflict (or Guard/Reserve on active duty during OIF/OEF or Desert Shield/Storm in a danger area) get 5 points added to a passing score. Veterans with a VA service-connected disability of at least 10%, disabled veterans over 55 receiving pension or compensation, certain spouses of disabled veterans, and unmarried widows/widowers of wartime veterans get 10 points instead. If no scored exam is used, the agency must give 'appropriate consideration' to eligible veterans. Preference does not apply to promotion, demotion, or transfer. Submit your DD-214 (and VA rating letter) with your application through Team Georgia Careers.
benefits.source_title: State Personnel Board Rule 478-1-.18 Veterans' Preference (rev. 11/28/2017), citing O.C.G.A. 45-2-20 to 45-2-22

benefits.benefit: Military Retirement Income Exclusion (VA compensation not taxed)
benefits.details: Georgia has an income tax. For tax years 2022-2026, retirees under 62 can exclude up to $17,500 of military retirement pay, plus another $17,500 if they have more than $17,500 of Georgia earned income; each spouse qualifies separately. Taxpayers 62-64 use the general retirement exclusion (up to $35,000) and 65+ up to $65,000, per GDVS. Under HB 266 (signed 2025), for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2027, anyone under 65 may exclude military retirement pay up to $65,000, but not on top of the general retirement exclusion. Claim it on your Georgia Form 500 using the DOR retirement income worksheet. VA disability compensation is not in federal adjusted gross income, which Georgia's return starts from, so it is not taxed; we did not find a Georgia page that states this directly.
benefits.source_title: DOR - Retirement Income Exclusion; HB 266 (2025) as passed House and Senate, O.C.G.A. 48-7-27(a)(5.1)

benefits.benefit: In-State Tuition Waiver for Recently Separated Veterans and Dependents (USG)
benefits.details: Board of Regents Policy 7.3.4.1 lets University System of Georgia schools waive out-of-state tuition for military personnel, recently separated service members, and National Guard members, and for students using VA education benefits ('covered individuals' under 38 U.S.C. 3679(c)), including some spouses and dependent children. A 2021 Chancellor's letter removed the old 36-month enrollment limit for covered individuals. Apply through your school's registrar with your DD-214 or VA Certificate of Eligibility; lawful presence verification is required. We could not retrieve the current policy text, so confirm details with the school.
benefits.source_title: University System of Georgia - Military Services and Benefits (Policy 7.3.4.1)

benefits.benefit: Georgia HERO Scholarship (Guard/Reserve combat service, children and spouses)
benefits.details: Up to $2,000 per academic year and up to $8,000 total for Georgia National Guard and U.S. Reserve members who deployed to a combat zone, for their children (generally 25 or younger during the service), and for children and spouses of a member who was killed, died, or 'became 100 percent disabled as a result of injuries' in a combat zone. You must meet Georgia residency for 12 consecutive months before the term and attend an eligible Georgia school. Awards are first-come, first-served as funds allow. Apply through the Georgia Student Finance Commission at GAfutures.org. This is not a general tuition waiver for disabled veterans or their dependents.
benefits.source_title: GSFC GAfutures - Georgia HERO Scholarship Eligibility and Award Amounts

benefits.benefit: Georgia War Veterans Homes (Augusta and Milledgeville)
benefits.details: State skilled nursing homes for wartime veterans who are current Georgia residents and lived in Georgia either the two years before applying or five of the past 15 years, served on active duty in a listed wartime period (WWII through Persian Gulf, August 2, 1990 to present), have an other-than-dishonorable discharge, and are VA-approved for skilled nursing care. A nominal daily fee is charged; for veterans rated 70% or higher service-connected, or admitted for a service-connected condition, VA pays the daily fee in full. Apply through the home's admissions office or any GDVS field office; waiting lists may exist.
