benefits.details: Veterans of the U.S. Armed Forces or Louisiana National Guard 'having a permanent service connected disability classification of fifty percent or more' get a free annual Disabled Veterans Hunting and Fishing License; the Louisiana Wildlife and Fisheries Foundation pays the $4 fee. It includes basic and saltwater fishing, basic, deer, waterfowl, and turkey hunting, and the WMA access permit, but not the federal duck stamp. Residents and nonresidents qualify. Apply in person at LDWF headquarters in Baton Rouge, by mail, or by email to lifetime@wlf.la.gov with the application, a copy of your driver license or ID, and VA proof of disability. Renew yearly. Since Act 321 of 2025 LDWF also issues a free durable hard card. Honorably discharged resident veterans without a 50% rating can buy a $20 hunting and fishing combination license (R.S. 56:3000(G), effective August 1, 2025).
benefits.source_title: R.S. 56:3000(H) Disabled/Special Needs Hunting and Fishing license; (G) Honorably Discharged Veteran license (Acts 2025, No. 321); LDWF Special Licenses and Permits page

benefits.benefit: Free day-use entry to Louisiana State Parks with the Disabled Veteran State Park Permit
benefits.details: A Louisiana resident veteran who has had a limb amputated, received a federal automobile allowance, or is rated by the VA or Social Security as totally and permanently disabled or at least 50 percent disabled 'shall be exempt from paying the day use entrance fee to any Louisiana state park.' Everyone riding with you in one private, non-commercial vehicle also enters free. Apply for the permit through your parish veterans service office; the Office of State Parks issues it after LDVA verifies eligibility. The permit does not discount camping or cabins; active duty and retired military get 15% off rentals with code MILITARY. State parks are run by the Office of State Parks (lastateparks.com, an official site that is not a .gov address).
benefits.source_title: R.S. 56:1694 Exemption from entrance fees; certain veterans (Acts 1980, No. 827; 1991, No. 372); Louisiana State Parks Special Rates and Discounts page; LDVA State Benefits page

benefits.benefit: Title 29 tuition and fee exemption for children and spouses of 90% to 100% or unemployable veterans
benefits.details: Minimum rating: 90% service-connected or rated unemployable. Children ages 16 to 25, and spouses or surviving spouses, of a veteran who was 'rated ninety percent or above' service-connected disabled or 'determined to be unemployable' by the VA, or who was killed in action, died in service, is MIA or POW, or died from a wartime service-connected disability, attend any Louisiana public college or university with no tuition, matriculation, registration, lab, athletic, medical, nonresident or other school fees. The veteran must have lived in Louisiana at least 12 months before entering service, before death, or before the child enrolls (or been permanently assigned to a Louisiana installation). Spouses must use it within 10 years of eligibility. Apply through your parish veterans service office; LDVA mails a certificate you give to the school. You cannot combine it with R.S. 17:1686 benefits.
benefits.source_title: R.S. 29:288 Educational benefits for children, spouses, and surviving spouses of veterans (as amended by Acts 2023, No. 46 and Acts 2024, No. 74); LDVA Title 29 page

benefits.benefit: In-state tuition for veterans and dependents using VA education benefits; National Guard tuition exemption
benefits.details: Louisiana public colleges classify a veteran, spouse, or dependent who is 'eligible to receive educational assistance administered by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs' as a resident for tuition and fees, with no prior Louisiana residency, for as long as the student stays continuously enrolled (LSU residency policy; the state statute cite was not retrieved). Louisiana National Guard members age 17 or older who are domiciled in Louisiana get free tuition at public colleges for five academic years or until a degree, and the clock pauses during mobilization (R.S. 29:36.1). Act 355 of 2026 lets veterans use a DD-214 as proof of eligibility for TOPS starting August 1, 2026. Apply at the school's registrar or veterans office.
benefits.source_title: Louisiana State University Office of the University Registrar - Residency Regulations (veterans section); R.S. 29:36.1 National Guard tuition exemption

benefits.benefit: Military retired pay and Survivor Benefit Plan exempt from state income tax; flat 3% rate since 2025
benefits.details: Income 'pursuant to a retirement system for retirees of the United States Government' is exempt from Louisiana income tax, which the Department of Revenue confirms covers military retired pay and 'a military survivor benefit plan.' VA disability compensation is not taxed because Louisiana starts from federal adjusted gross income. Beginning with tax year 2025, Act 11 of the 2024 Third Extraordinary Session replaced the graduated brackets with a flat 3% rate and raised the standard deduction to $12,500 single or $25,000 joint, indexed for inflation from 2026. Report the exempt retirement income on Schedule E of Form IT-540. There is no extra deduction tied to a disability rating.
benefits.source_title: Louisiana Department of Revenue FAQ - Retirement benefits excluded from Louisiana income tax (R.S. 47:44.2); Revenue Information Bulletin 25-012 (March 7, 2025, Act 11 of 2024 3rd E.S.)

benefits.benefit: Veterans preference points in state and city civil service hiring (10 points disabled, 5 points wartime)
benefits.details: The Louisiana Constitution requires state and city civil service to add 10 points to the passing score of 'each honorably discharged veteran who served either in peace or in war and who has one or more disabilities recognized as service-connected' by the VA, and to certain spouses, unremarried widows, and parents; only one 10-point preference per person. Veterans who served in a declared war, a campaign with an authorized badge, or at least 90 days after September 11, 2001 (not for training) get 5 points. Points apply only to original (probational or job) appointments and only if you reach the minimum score. Claim the points on your state application (SF-10); for 10 points attach your DD-214 and a VA disability letter dated within the last 6 months. Spouses and parents use Form C.S. 295. Preference employees also have layoff protection.
benefits.source_title: Louisiana Constitution Art. X, Sec. 10(A)(2) Veterans; State Civil Service HR Handbook Procedure 22 - Veterans Preference Information (rev. 3/22/18)

benefits.benefit: Louisiana Veterans Homes (five) with no monthly fee for 70% or higher service-connected veterans
benefits.details: LDVA runs homes in Jackson, Monroe, Bossier City, Reserve, and Jennings. Louisiana veterans who were honorably discharged and served 90 days of active duty (wartime or peacetime), eligible National Guard members and reservists (Act 132 of 2025 added Guard veterans who never deployed on federal orders), spouses of veterans, and Gold Star parents may apply. Veterans 'with a VA service-connected rating of 70% or higher,' or admitted for a condition related to their service connection at any rating, live there free. Other veterans pay a monthly fee ($2,424 as posted, changes yearly, often offset by VA Aid and Attendance); spouses and Gold Star parents pay $5,500 per month. Submit the admissions application with a pre-admission medical exam.
benefits.source_title: LDVA - Louisiana Veterans Homes (admissions requirements and fees); LDVA 2025 Regular Session summary (Acts 132 and 191 of 2025)

benefits.benefit: Free burial in five state veterans cemeteries; Military Family Assistance Fund grants up to $10,000
benefits.details: Veterans who served active duty (not training only) and were discharged under honorable conditions are buried free in the state cemeteries at Leesville, Rayville, Keithville, Slidell, or Jennings; spouses and dependent children pay a fee equal to the federal VA plot allowance. Pre-need registration is optional and can be done online. Separately, the Military Family Assistance (MFA) Fund pays up to $10,000 in a 12-month period to current Louisiana resident veterans with an honorable or under-honorable-conditions discharge (and Guard and Reserve members in good standing) for rent or mortgage, utilities, car payments, food, and some medical bills when there is a documented hardship; it is a fund of last resort reviewed at a monthly board meeting. Act 241 of 2025 added indigent veteran burials and up to $1,000 in education help for children of certain disabled veterans. Apply online or by mail to LDVA.
benefits.source_title: LDVA - Louisiana Veterans Cemeteries; LDVA - Military Family Assistance Fund; Act 241 of 2025 (HB 116)

states.name: Maine
notes: Maine's veteran property tax exemption is small: $6,000 of just value, not a full exemption. For the disability path the law says you must receive federal pension or compensation for 'total disability.' Maine Revenue Services Bulletin No. 7 (October 14, 2025) adds that a veteran 'receiving compensation as unemployable at the 100% level is considered totally disabled,' so TDIU (total disability based on individual unemployability) counts. Permanence is not required. A 100% schedular rating also counts.

The war-period rule matters. If you served during a federally recognized war period (or earned an expeditionary medal, or served February 1, 1955 to February 27, 1961), you qualify at age 62 or when you receive federal pension or compensation for total disability, service-connected or not. If you did not serve in a war period, you qualify only if you receive federal pension or compensation for a total service-connected disability.

File a written application and proof with the assessor of the town where you live by April 1 of the first year you want the exemption. In the unorganized territory you file with the State Tax Assessor. Once approved you do not refile each year unless the assessor asks. Your application is confidential. The dollar amount is multiplied by your town's certified assessment ratio, so a $6,000 exemption at an 85% ratio is $5,100 off assessed value; some towns make up the difference under 36 M.R.S. 6234.

Big change coming. The 2026 supplemental budget (Public Law 2025, chapter 650, Part M) ends the separate veteran exemption in 36 M.R.S. 653 for tax years beginning on or after April 1, 2027. It is replaced by a consolidated homestead exemption in 36 M.R.S. 683-A: $25,000 for every homestead plus a veteran add-on that scales with your VA rating ($10,000 at 60%, $20,000 at 70%, $30,000 at 80%, $40,000 at 90%, $50,000 at 100%; $5,000 to $7,000 for veterans under 60%). Property that had the exemption on April 1, 2026 is presumed eligible for the equivalent exemption in 2027. Maine Revenue Services must publish transition guidance; as of this research it had not.

Surviving spouse rules: an unremarried surviving spouse or minor child gets the same $6,000 exemption if the veteran would have qualified, or if the survivor receives a federal pension or compensation as a survivor. A widowed parent age 62 or older receiving federal benefits for a child's service-connected death also qualifies. The survivor must be a Maine resident; the home must be the survivor's residence. If the veteran died in the 12 months before April 1, an assessor may abate taxes for a survivor who applies within one year of commitment.

Disabled Veteran license plates need VA certification 'as to the veteran's permanent disability and receipt of 100% service-connected benefits.' The BMV says the disability must be permanent and total. The plate waives the registration fee and title fee for up to 3 vehicles, and a disability placard is free. The excise tax exemption (paid to your town) is separate: it applies to up to 3 owned vehicles, and from July 1, 2026 up to 3 leased vehicles, for veterans receiving federal pension or compensation for 'total, service-connected disability,' whether or not you take the DV plate. Your name must be on the title or lease. If you choose a different plate you pay the regular registration fee. No official source says how TDIU is treated for the plate.

Hunting, fishing and trapping licenses are free for life at a 50% or higher service-connected rating with an honorable discharge, and they now include most permits (bear, turkey, migratory bird, pheasant, muzzleloader, crossbow, archery, coyote night hunt, and expanded-archery deer permits). Lottery permits like moose and antlerless deer still require applying. Residents of states with reciprocal agreements can get the Maine license too. The same 50% rule waives the fee for a noncommercial lobster and crab license and a scallop license through the Department of Marine Resources.

Every honorably discharged Maine resident veteran gets a free lifetime day-use pass to state parks, historic sites and the Maine State Museum (apply by mail with your DD-214; veterans 65 and older are not issued the pass because seniors already enter free). Free camping and shelter fees are a separate benefit tied to the Disabled Veteran plate: you must send your BMV letter to the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry to be added to the Disabled Veterans' Camping List. The passes are not valid at Baxter State Park, Acadia National Park, the Allagash Wilderness Waterway, Penobscot River Corridor, Penobscot Narrows Observatory or Maine Wildlife Park.

The Veterans Dependents Educational Benefits tuition waiver uses the words 'total permanent disability resulting from a service-connected disability.' A 100% rating that is not permanent, or TDIU, does not match that wording. The veteran must have entered service from Maine or lived in Maine 5 years before applying, and must keep living in Maine while the dependent uses it. Children must be 16 to 22 (up to 26 if their own military service delayed them), get 120 credit hours over 10 years, keep a 2.0 GPA, and must apply for a Pell Grant. Spouses get 120 credit hours including master's programs. Room and board are not covered.

Maine income tax: military retirement pay and Survivor Benefit Plan payments have been fully exempt since tax year 2016, and starting with tax year 2026 the exemption covers all uniformed services (adds NOAA Corps and Public Health Service). VA disability compensation is not in federal adjusted gross income, which is where the Maine return starts, so Maine does not tax it. Separately, a veteran rated 100% for service-connected disabilities 'that are rated permanent' gets double the Property Tax Fairness Credit on the Maine income tax return (36 M.R.S. 5219-KK(2-E)); the regular credit cap is $1,500 under age 65 and $2,000 at 65 or older for 2026.

State hiring preference is a guaranteed interview, not points. Any veteran with a discharge other than dishonorable who meets the minimum qualifications must be offered an interview for a classified state job, and veterans are kept first in layoffs with equal seniority. A 2026 law (Public Law 2025, chapter 634) extended this to spouses of current service members and Guard or Reserve members. There is no extra preference for disabled veterans.

Not available or not found: Maine has no full property tax exemption for 100% disabled veterans (the largest current exemption is $6,000, or $50,000 for a specially adapted housing unit). No driver's license fee waiver for disabled veterans was found in Maine law. No state veterans bonus program was found. Maine Veterans' Homes are run by a state-created nonprofit; admission requires Maine residency at entry into service or at application and is not limited to disabled veterans.

benefits.benefit: Veteran property tax exemption: $6,000 of just value (36 M.R.S. 653(1)(C))
benefits.details: Maine exempts up to $6,000 of just value of the home where you live. You qualify if you served during a federally recognized war period (including Korea, Vietnam, Persian Gulf, OEF, OIF, New Dawn, or February 1, 1955 to February 27, 1961, or you hold an expeditionary medal) and are 62 or older or receive any federal pension or compensation for total disability, service-connected or not. Veterans with no war-period service qualify if they receive federal pension or compensation for a total, service-connected disability. Maine Revenue Services says a veteran paid as unemployable at the 100% level (TDIU) counts as totally disabled; permanence is not required. You must be a Maine resident with a discharge other than dishonorable. File a written application and proof (DD-214, VA letter) with your town assessor by April 1 of the first year; the amount is adjusted by the town's certified ratio. This exemption ends after the tax year beginning April 1, 2026 and is replaced by 36 M.R.S. 683-A.
benefits.source_title: Maine Legislature - 36 M.R.S. 653 Estates of veterans; Maine Revenue Services Property Tax Bulletin No. 7 (Oct. 14, 2025)

benefits.benefit: $50,000 property tax exemption for a specially adapted housing unit (36 M.R.S. 653(1)(D-1))
benefits.details: If you are a war-period or expeditionary-medal veteran described in 38 U.S.C. 2101 and you received a federal Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant, up to $50,000 of the just value of that specially adapted home is exempt. Maine Revenue Services describes the veteran as totally and permanently disabled, which matches the federal SAH grant rules. Your unremarried surviving spouse keeps the exemption. You cannot stack this with the $6,000 exemption. Apply with your town assessor by April 1 with your DD-214 and the VA letter showing total and permanent disability and the SAH grant. The exemption is adjusted by the town's certified ratio. Under the 2027 consolidated homestead law (36 M.R.S. 683-A(2)(E)) SAH grant recipients keep a $50,000 add-on.
benefits.source_title: Maine Legislature - 36 M.R.S. 653(1)(D-1) Estates of veterans, specially adapted housing; MRS Bulletin No. 7

benefits.benefit: $6,000 property tax exemption for surviving spouses, minor children and widowed parents (36 M.R.S. 653(1)(D))
benefits.details: An unremarried surviving spouse or minor child of a veteran who would have qualified for the veteran exemption, or who receives a federal pension or compensation as the survivor of a veteran, gets up to $6,000 of just value exempt on the home where they live. A widowed parent age 62 or older who receives federal pension or compensation based on a child's service-connected death also gets $6,000. The survivor must be a Maine resident and not remarried. Apply with the town assessor by April 1 with the death certificate, the veteran's DD-214 and the federal benefit letter. If the veteran died within the 12 months before April 1, the assessor may abate taxes for a survivor who applies within one year of the tax commitment date. After April 1, 2027 survivors get the add-on the veteran would have received under 36 M.R.S. 683-A.
benefits.source_title: Maine Legislature - 36 M.R.S. 653(1)(D) Estates of veterans, surviving spouse, minor child, parent; MRS Bulletin No. 7

benefits.benefit: Consolidated homestead exemption with tiered veteran add-on, tax years from April 1, 2027 (36 M.R.S. 683-A)
benefits.details: Starting with the property tax year that begins April 1, 2027, Maine replaces the veteran exemption with one homestead exemption of $25,000 of just value plus a veteran add-on based on your VA service-connected rating: up to $10,000 at 60%, $20,000 at 70%, $30,000 at 80%, $40,000 at 90% and $50,000 at 100%. Veterans with no rating or under 60% get $5,000 (under age 62), $6,000 (62 or older) or $7,000 (World War I era). SAH grant recipients get a $50,000 add-on. Only one add-on tier applies. Unremarried surviving spouses, minor children and qualifying parents get the add-on the veteran would have received. You must be a Maine permanent resident who owned the homestead for the preceding 12 months, and the amount is adjusted by the town's assessment ratio. File written application and proof of entitlement with your town assessor by April 1. The law says property that had the old exemption on April 1, 2026 is presumed eligible for the equivalent exemption in 2027; Maine Revenue Services must issue transition guidance, which was not yet published.
benefits.source_title: Maine Legislature - 36 M.R.S. 683-A Homestead exemption (enacted by PL 2025, c. 650, Pt. M, L.D. 2212)

benefits.benefit: Disabled Veteran plates: no registration or title fee, free placard, excise tax exemption up to 3 vehicles
benefits.details: The Secretary of State issues Disabled Veteran plates and a registration certificate with no annual registration fee to any 100% disabled veteran who provides VA or service branch certification of permanent disability and receipt of 100% service-connected benefits; the BMV states the disability must be permanent and total. Up to 3 vehicles (registered weight 26,000 lbs or less) qualify, a disability placard is free on request, and the BMV also waives title fees. Veterans who lost both legs or the use of both legs, and amputee or blind veterans with a VA-furnished or specially designed vehicle, pay no motor vehicle fees at all, including sales tax. Separately, the municipal excise tax is waived on up to 3 automobiles you own (and from July 1, 2026 up to 3 you lease) if you receive federal pension or compensation for total, service-connected disability, whether or not you display the DV plate; your name must appear on the title or lease. Bring your DD-214 and current VA Benefit Summary letter to your town office or BMV branch. If you choose a different plate you pay the normal registration fee. TDIU is not mentioned in the plate statute.
benefits.source_title: Maine Legislature - 29-A M.R.S. 523 Certain veterans (amended PL 2025, c. 152); 36 M.R.S. 1483(12), (12-A); Maine BMV Available Veteran Plates

benefits.benefit: Purple Heart plates at no fee, Special Veteran plates, and Veteran designation on the driver's license
benefits.details: Purple Heart recipients get Purple Heart registration plates at no registration fee for up to 2 vehicles (10,000 lbs or less); you still pay excise tax. An unremarried surviving spouse may keep using the plates. Medal of Honor, former prisoner of war and Pearl Harbor survivor plates are also fee-free. Any honorably discharged veteran may buy Special Veteran plates ($35 to $37 for passenger vehicles) with one of 35 commemorative decals, or a Disability Special Veteran plate with Form PS-18. Any veteran with an honorable discharge can add a military service designation (flag) to a Maine driver's license or ID card by showing a DD-214 or VA certification; it is free at renewal or $5 for a duplicate card between renewals.
benefits.source_title: Maine Legislature - 29-A M.R.S. 524 Other special veterans registration plates; 29-A M.R.S. 1412 Military service designation; Maine BMV Available Veteran Plates

benefits.benefit: Free lifetime hunting, fishing and trapping licenses at 50%+; free noncommercial lobster and scallop licenses
benefits.details: A veteran honorably discharged from the Armed Forces or National Guard with a service-connected disability evaluated at 50% or more gets, at no cost, all hunting, trapping and fishing licenses, including permits and stamps (bear, migratory bird, pheasant, turkey, muzzleloader, crossbow, archery, coyote night hunt, and one antlerless and one either-sex expanded-archery deer permit), plus a guide license if qualified. The license lasts for life as long as you stay a resident of Maine or a reciprocal state and it is not revoked. Residents of New Hampshire, Vermont, Rhode Island, Texas and other reciprocal states may apply. Lottery permits such as moose and antlerless deer still require an application; the Bureau also runs a Disabled Veterans' Controlled Moose Hunt and donated moose permit lottery for veterans rated 50% or higher. Apply with the Disabled Veteran License Application and proof of residency and rating at any Bureau of Veterans' Services office or by mail. Maine residents at 50% or higher also pay no fee for a noncommercial lobster and crab license or a scallop license from the Department of Marine Resources.
benefits.source_title: Maine Legislature - 12 M.R.S. 10853(4) Complimentary and reduced-rate licenses, disabled veteran (amended PL 2025, c. 333); 12 M.R.S. 6421(7-D); Maine IF&W Licenses for Persons with Disabilities

benefits.benefit: Free Lifetime Veteran State Park and Museum Pass; free park entry and camping with Disabled Veteran plates
benefits.details: Any Maine resident veteran with an honorable or general-under-honorable discharge gets a free lifetime day-use pass to Maine State Parks, historic sites and the Maine State Museum. Mail the application and a copy of your DD-214 to the Bureau of Veterans' Services; allow 2 to 3 weeks. The pass is for the veteran only; veterans 65 and older are not issued one because Maine seniors already enter free. Separately, a veteran whose vehicle displays Disabled Veteran plates or placards (100% permanent and total, or double leg loss) pays no admission at any state-owned park, camping area or beach, and the veteran, spouse and unmarried children are exempt from family camping and shelter reservation fees (limit 6 per site, veteran must be present). To get the camping waiver, send your BMV Disabled Veteran plate letter to the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry to be placed on the Disabled Veterans' Camping List. Neither benefit is valid at Baxter State Park, Acadia National Park, the Allagash Wilderness Waterway, Penobscot River Corridor, Penobscot Narrows Observatory or Maine Wildlife Park.
benefits.source_title: Maine Bureau of Veterans' Services - Free Lifetime Veteran State Park and Museum Pass; BVS Free Camping for Disabled Veterans; 12 M.R.S. 1819

benefits.benefit: Veterans Dependents Educational Benefits: 100% tuition waiver for children and spouses (37-B M.R.S. 505)
benefits.details: Maine waives 100% of tuition and mandatory fees at the University of Maine System, Maine Community College System and Maine Maritime Academy for the child or spouse of a veteran who has a total permanent disability resulting from a service-connected disability, was killed in action, died from a service-connected disability, was totally and permanently disabled from a service-connected disability at death, or has been missing, captured or detained more than 90 days. The veteran must have entered service from Maine or lived in Maine for 5 years before the application, and must keep living in Maine while benefits are used. Children must be at least 16, a high school graduate, and start before age 22 (26 if their own military service delayed them); they get up to 120 credit hours over 10 years for certificate, associate or bachelor programs and must keep a 2.0 GPA. Spouses (current spouse, or unremarried widow or widower) get 120 credit hours including master's programs. Room and board are not covered. Every student must apply for a federal Pell Grant. Apply through the Bureau of Veterans' Services with the program application.
benefits.source_title: Maine Bureau of Veterans' Services - Veterans Dependents Educational Benefits; 37-B M.R.S. 505(2)

benefits.benefit: In-state tuition for all honorably discharged veterans at Maine public colleges (20-A M.R.S. 10010)
benefits.details: If you are a current member of the Armed Forces or an honorably discharged veteran enrolled at any University of Maine System campus, Maine Community College System campus or Maine Maritime Academy, you pay in-state tuition regardless of your state of residence. No disability rating or waiting period is required. Show your DD-214 (or GI Bill certificate of eligibility or military ID) to the school's registrar or veterans office when you enroll.
benefits.source_title: Maine Legislature - 20-A M.R.S. 10010 Current members and veterans of the United States Armed Forces

benefits.benefit: Military retirement pay and Survivor Benefit Plan fully exempt from Maine income tax; VA pay not taxed
benefits.details: Since tax year 2016 all benefits under a military retirement plan, including survivor benefits, are fully exempt from Maine income tax, with no cap and no reduction for Social Security. Starting with tax year 2026 the definition covers all uniformed services (adds NOAA Corps and Public Health Service to Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines, Coast Guard and Space Force). Survivor Benefit Plan annuities paid to the survivor of a member who died from service are also subtracted. Claim the subtraction on Form 1040ME Schedule 1S and the pension income deduction worksheet. VA disability compensation, DIC and pension are excluded from federal adjusted gross income, which is the starting point of the Maine return, so Maine does not tax them. Other pension income has a separate capped deduction ($48,216 per person for 2025) with an income phaseout.
benefits.source_title: Maine Revenue Services - Individual Income Tax FAQ, pension income deduction (revised April 13, 2026); 36 M.R.S. 5122(2)(M-2), (HH); MRS 2025 Legislative Changes

benefits.benefit: Property Tax Fairness Credit doubled for 100% permanently and totally disabled veterans (36 M.R.S. 5219-KK)
benefits.details: Maine's Property Tax Fairness Credit is a refundable income tax credit for property tax or rent paid on your Maine homestead that exceeds 4% of your income. A resident veteran rated by the VA at 100% for one or more service-connected disabilities that are rated permanent gets an additional credit equal to the regular credit, so the credit is doubled. For 2026 the regular credit is capped at $1,500 under age 65 and $2,000 at 65 or older; the combined credit cannot exceed the property tax and rent you actually paid. On a joint return only one spouse must be the 100% permanent and total veteran. Claim it on Schedule PTFC/STFC with your Form 1040ME; the benefit base (property tax or rent counted) is capped by filing status.
benefits.source_title: Maine Legislature - 36 M.R.S. 5219-KK Property tax fairness credit, sub-§2-D and 2-E (amended PL 2025, c. 650)

benefits.benefit: Veteran preference in state hiring: guaranteed interview and layoff retention (5 M.R.S. 7054-B)
benefits.details: For any classified State of Maine job, the hiring agency must offer an interview to any veteran who meets the minimum qualifications. 'Veteran' means anyone who served on active duty in the Armed Forces, Reserves or National Guard and received a discharge other than dishonorable. In a reduction in force, veterans are retained ahead of other employees with equal seniority, status and performance reviews. Gold star spouses have the same preference, and a 2026 law (PL 2025, c. 634) added spouses of current active duty, Reserve and National Guard members. Maine does not add points for disabled veterans. Claim the preference when you apply through the Bureau of Human Resources; if you are not hired, BHR will point you to other openings under Executive Order 2016-002.
benefits.source_title: Maine Legislature - 5 M.R.S. 7054-B Veteran preference (amended PL 2025, c. 634); Maine BVS Employment page

benefits.benefit: Veterans Emergency Financial Assistance Program grants up to $2,000 (37-B M.R.S. 505(1-C))
benefits.details: A Maine resident veteran with an honorable or general-under-honorable discharge who has an emergency and no savings or other help may get a grant of up to $2,000 for things like preventing homelessness, home damage from fire or flood not covered by insurance, illness of the veteran or a family member, vehicle repair to keep a job, or up to $500 for a dental emergency. A separate $2,000 grant is available while a VA pension claim is pending. Reserve retirees and, case by case, Maine National Guard members may also qualify. The Bureau runs the program through a contracted vendor (Fedcap Veterans Forward, 844-653-0316); denials can be reconsidered by the director and commissioner.
benefits.source_title: Maine Bureau of Veterans' Services - Tax Exemptions and Financial Benefits (VEFAP); 37-B M.R.S. 505(1-C)

benefits.benefit: Maine Veterans' Homes (six locations) and free burial in the Maine Veterans' Memorial Cemetery System
benefits.details: Maine Veterans' Homes, a state-chartered nonprofit, runs six homes in Augusta, Bangor, Caribou, Machias, Scarborough and South Paris offering long-term, short-term, skilled and rehabilitative care. Admission is limited to veterans who were Maine residents when they entered the Armed Forces or are Maine residents when they apply, plus their spouses, widows or widowers, and gold star parents; admission is granted when private pay, Medicare or Medicaid rules are met. Burial in the four state veterans cemeteries (two in Augusta, Caribou, Springvale) is free for eligible veterans (honorable or general discharge; 24 continuous months of service if enlisted after September 7, 1980) and their spouses and eligible dependent children; headstones and vaults are not provided by the State. Schedule through the cemetery office at 207-287-3481.
benefits.source_title: Maine Legislature - 37-B M.R.S. 607 Maine Veterans' Homes admission; 37-B M.R.S. 504 Maine Veterans' Memorial Cemetery System; BVS Preparing for Burial

states.name: Maryland

agency.name: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families

notes: The full state property tax exemption (Tax-Property 7-208) is for a veteran the VA has declared to have a 'permanent 100% service connected disability' that is 'reasonably certain to continue for the life of the veteran.' The state assessment agency (SDAT) also accepts a rating that is 'permanently unemployable,' based on a 1976 Attorney General opinion, so a permanent TDIU rating counts. A temporary 100% rating does not. The VA Summary of Benefits letter is not accepted; you need the rating decision or the VA certification on the SDAT form.

File the SDAT 'Application for Exemption for Disabled Veterans' with the Supervisor of Assessments in the county where the home is. There is no deadline; you can file any time. If you file within 30 days after settlement on a new home, the tax is abated from the settlement date. You can even apply before you buy; SDAT must answer within 15 business days. Refunds of past tax are allowed only if you apply within 3 years of the calendar year you first became eligible, and no refunds go back before the 2018-2019 tax year.

You must own the home and it must be your legal residence (principal residence) with no more than two families living there. You must be a Maryland resident; SDAT asks for a Maryland driver's license, voter card, or last year's Maryland tax return as proof. There is no income cap.

A surviving spouse keeps the exemption only while unmarried and only while owning and living in the home. The spouse can move the same dollar amount of exemption to a new home. A spouse who remarries and later divorces does not get it back. Surviving spouses of members who died in the line of duty and spouses who receive VA Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) also qualify. Since June 1, 2026 (Chapter 647), the old 2-year limit to buy a home after a line-of-duty death is gone.

Veterans rated 50% to 99% get nothing from the state exemption. Instead, counties and cities may offer a local credit under Tax-Property 9-265: 25% off the county tax for 50% to 74% ratings and 50% off for 75% or higher (or a non-permanent 100% rating). The law also lets counties limit by income. The state's $100,000 federal AGI cap was repealed on June 1, 2026 (Chapter 646), and each county now sets its own income rule. You apply to the county, usually every year (Anne Arundel by April 1; Frederick by October 1). Not every county offers it.

Vehicle registration fees are waived for one or more vehicles owned and personally used by a veteran the VA has classified as having 'lost the use of a hand, arm, or leg, or is totally disabled,' or who is legally blind. MVA applies this to veterans rated 100% and gives them a free Disabled Veteran plate and permanent registration. Veterans rated 50% to 99% (including an 'unemployability rating') get the plate free but still pay the yearly registration fee. Bills to add a fee waiver for TDIU veterans (SB 179 and HB 248 in 2025, HB 844 in 2026) did not pass.

Maryland has no state driver license fee waiver for disabled veterans, no vehicle excise (sales) tax exemption for disabled veterans, and no veteran-specific parking placard. The free 'VETERAN' designation on a driver license is open to any veteran with an honorable, general, or general under honorable conditions discharge.

Free lifetime hunting and fishing licenses are for Maryland residents who are 100% service-connected disabled, former prisoners of war, or 'deemed unemployable' by the VA. You must apply at a DNR Licensing and Registration Service Center with your VA letter. Yearly federal and state migratory bird stamps and the Big Game Harvest Record are not included. Every veteran, from any state, gets free day-use entry to Maryland State Parks; there is no veteran discount on the $75 annual Passport.

Maryland taxes military retired pay, but you can subtract the first $12,500 if you are under 55 and the first $20,000 if you are 55 or older (Tax-General 10-207(q)). A 2026 bill (HB 857) to raise the under-55 amount to $20,000 did not pass. VA disability compensation is not in federal adjusted gross income, and Maryland starts from federal AGI, so it is not taxed; no Maryland page says this in so many words.

State hiring: every honorably discharged veteran gets 10 points added to a passing selection test score. The spouse of a veteran with a service-connected disability and the surviving spouse of a veteran also get 10 points. Former prisoners of war get 2 more points. Maryland law no longer gives extra points for a service-connected disability itself; a separate 5-point credit exists for anyone with a disability under the ADA.

The Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship pays up to $13,689 (2025-2026) at a Maryland school. It covers veterans rated 25% or more who have used up federal education benefits, and children and unremarried spouses of service members who died or have a 'service-connected 100% permanent disability.' Apply through the school's financial aid office by July 15. For 2026-2027, MHEC sends the money to the schools, which may change awards.

benefits.benefit: Full property tax exemption on the home of a 100% permanently disabled veteran (Tax-Property 7-208)
benefits.details: Your home (the house, yard, and needed structures, with no more than two families living there) is fully exempt from state, county, and city property tax if you were honorably discharged and the VA has declared you to have a 'permanent 100% service connected disability' that is 'reasonably certain to continue for the life of the veteran.' SDAT also accepts a permanent unemployability (TDIU) rating under a 1976 Attorney General opinion. You must own the home, live in it as your legal residence, and be a Maryland resident. File SDAT's Application for Exemption for Disabled Veterans (Rev. Feb 2025) with your county Supervisor of Assessments any time, with your DD-214, your VA rating decision showing the effective date (the Summary of Benefits letter is not accepted), and proof of Maryland residency. Apply within 30 days of settlement to have tax abated from the settlement date; apply within 3 years of becoming eligible to get refunds of tax already paid. Disabled active duty members with a lifelong service-connected physical disability qualify too but must recertify yearly.
benefits.source_title: Maryland General Assembly - Tax-Property Article 7-208 (Disabled active duty service members, disabled veterans, and surviving spouses); SDAT Real Property Exemptions page and Application for Exemption for Disabled Veterans

benefits.benefit: Property tax exemption for the surviving spouse of a disabled veteran, line-of-duty death, or DIC recipient
benefits.details: If you are the unremarried surviving spouse of a veteran who had (or posthumously qualifies for) a permanent 100% service-connected rating, you keep the full exemption on the home as long as you own and live in it. If the veteran never applied but was living in Maryland at death, you can still apply. If you sell and buy another Maryland home, the same dollar amount of exemption moves with you. The exemption also covers the unremarried surviving spouse of a service member who died in the line of duty (the home must have been owned by the member, or bought by the spouse if either of you was domiciled in Maryland at the death; the former 2-year purchase limit was repealed effective June 1, 2026) and anyone receiving VA Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC). File SDAT's Application for Exemption for Surviving Spouses of a Disabled Veteran (Rev. Feb 2025) with the county Supervisor of Assessments, with the veteran's DD-214 and VA rating decision, your proof of Maryland residency, and the death certificate. Refunds are limited to 3 years from the calendar year you became eligible. A spouse who remarries and later divorces does not regain the exemption.
benefits.source_title: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation - Real Property Exemptions (Tax-Property 7-208(c), (g); 2026 Md. Laws ch. 647)

benefits.benefit: County or city property tax credit for veterans rated 50% to 99% (Tax-Property 9-265; local option)
benefits.details: If your county or city has adopted this credit, you get 25% off the county (or city) property tax on your home if the VA rates you 'at least 50% but not more than 74%,' and 50% off if you are rated 'at least 75%' and do not qualify for the full state exemption. The law covers a 'permanent service-connected disability of at least 50%' or a 'nonpermanent service-connected disability of 100%,' but a county may limit it to permanent ratings. You must be honorably discharged, own the home, and live there as your legal residence with no more than two families. Until June 30, 2026 the state capped eligibility at $100,000 federal adjusted gross income; starting with tax years after that date (Chapter 646 of 2026) each county sets its own income rule, so check locally. Apply to the county finance or treasury office, not SDAT, with your DD-214, VA award letter, Maryland ID, and tax return; most counties require a new application every year (Anne Arundel by April 1; Frederick by October 1). Counties may extend the credit to unremarried surviving spouses. The state veterans agency lists Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Calvert, Cecil, Frederick, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Washington counties as having a local veteran credit, but terms differ (Howard County's version is an age-65-plus credit of 20% for 75% to 99% ratings) and the list may be incomplete.
benefits.source_title: Maryland General Assembly - Tax-Property Article 9-265 (Property tax credit for dwelling house of disabled veterans); 2026 Md. Laws ch. 646 (HB 1611); DVMF Local Property Tax Exemptions page

benefits.benefit: Vehicle registration fee exemption, free Disabled Veteran plates, and permanent registration
benefits.details: State law (Transportation 13-903(a)(8)) exempts from registration fees any vehicle 'owned by, or leased to, and personally used by a veteran' whom the VA has classified as having 'lost the use of a hand, arm, or leg, or is totally disabled,' or who is legally blind (20/200 or a 20-degree field). The surviving spouse of a disabled veteran as defined in Tax-Property 7-208 is also exempt (13-903(a)(9)). MVA applies this to veterans rated 100%: you pay no registration fee, get Disabled Veteran plates (with or without the wheelchair symbol) at no charge, and your registration and sticker are permanent with no renewal trips. Veterans with a 'service-connected disability rating or unemployability rating of 50-99%' get the Disabled Veteran plate free but still pay annual registration fees and the surcharge. Vanity or organizational plates cost their normal plate fee. Book an appointment through myMVA (or mail form VR-120) and bring a letter on Maryland DVMF letterhead or a VA letter showing your rating. The law does not state a vehicle limit. Whether a TDIU rating counts as 'totally disabled' for the fee waiver is not stated by MVA; bills to add TDIU veterans (2025 SB 179/HB 248, 2026 HB 844) did not pass.
benefits.source_title: MDOT Motor Vehicle Administration - Military Service Members: License Plates (Transportation Article 13-903(a)(8)-(9), 13-903(d)); MVA brochure DL-401

benefits.benefit: Free 'VETERAN' designation on a Maryland driver license or ID card
benefits.details: Any veteran who served on active duty (not only for training) and has an Honorable, General, or General under honorable conditions discharge can have the word VETERAN printed on the front of a Maryland driver license or ID card. There is no cost if you add it without making other changes; normal fees apply if you renew or change your name or address at the same time. Schedule an MVA appointment through myMVA and bring one document such as a DD-214, Veteran Health Identification Card, VA letter, DVMF letter, or DD Form 2 retiree card. Maryland has no driver license fee waiver, no vehicle excise tax exemption, and no veteran-specific parking placard for disabled veterans.
benefits.source_title: MDOT Motor Vehicle Administration - Veteran Driver's License Designation

benefits.benefit: Complimentary lifetime hunting license and lifetime fishing license (100% disabled, TDIU, or former POW)
benefits.details: Maryland residents who are '100% service-connected disabled veterans or former prisoners of war or are deemed unemployable by the US Department of Veterans Affairs' can get a free lifetime hunting license and a free lifetime fishing license from the Department of Natural Resources. The hunting license includes the bow stamp, muzzleloader stamp, sika deer stamp, and furbearer permit; you still must buy the Maryland Migratory Game Bird Stamp, the federal duck stamp, and the Big Game Harvest Record each year. The fishing license includes the nontidal angler's license, trout stamp, Chesapeake Bay sport fishing license, and recreational oyster license. Send a VA letter of disability or VA certification with the signed Hunting License Application (H699) or Fishing License Application (DNRF3) to a DNR Licensing and Registration Service Center; the licenses are issued only at those centers. Purple Heart recipients get 50% off regular licenses. Questions: 410-260-3220.
benefits.source_title: Maryland Department of Natural Resources - Military One-Stop Shop (Military Veterans, Members, and POWs)

benefits.benefit: Free day-use entry to Maryland State Parks for all veterans
benefits.details: 'All applicable day-use entrance charges are waived for all veterans of the United States Armed Forces,' and the waiver 'applies to both resident and out-of-state veterans.' It covers only the veteran, not others in the car, unless the park charges a per-vehicle fee, in which case that fee is waived. Other service charges such as camping, boat launch, and rentals are not waived. The Park Service does not list a specific proof document; the free VETERAN designation on a Maryland driver license is suggested. Active duty members and Maryland National Guard members get the same waiver by showing a military ID. The $75 annual Maryland State Park and Trail Passport ($100 nonresident) covers everyone in the vehicle but has no veteran discount. Maryland has no free lifetime park pass for disabled veterans.
benefits.source_title: Maryland Park Service (DNR) - Veterans Admission Waiver

benefits.benefit: Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship (veterans 25%+; dependents of 100% permanent or deceased members)
benefits.details: This state scholarship pays up to $13,689 for 2025-2026 (capped at in-state tuition and mandatory fees at the highest-cost University System of Maryland four-year school) for study at a Maryland college, graduate program, or private career school. You qualify as a veteran with a 'service-connected disability of 25% or greater' who has used up or lost eligibility for federal veterans' education benefits, or as the child, stepchild, or unremarried surviving spouse of a service member who died from military service or has a 'service-connected 100% permanent disability' from it. Children and surviving spouses of 9/11 victims, Vietnam POW/MIA families, and certain public safety and school employees are also covered. You must be a Maryland resident when you apply and at least 16. Apply to your school's financial aid office (not MHEC) by July 15; awards renew automatically for up to 5 years full time or 8 years part time. Starting in 2026-2027 MHEC allocates funds to the schools, which may adjust awards.
benefits.source_title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program

benefits.benefit: Douglas J.J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship
benefits.details: If you served in Afghanistan on or after October 24, 2001, or Iraq on or after March 19, 2003 (as a veteran, active duty member, or activated Reserve or Maryland National Guard member), or you are the child, stepchild, or spouse of someone who did, you can get up to $8,699 a year (on campus), $5,637 (off campus), or $5,067 (living with parents) for 2025-2026 toward an undergraduate degree or a transferable 2-year certificate at a Maryland school. You must be a Maryland resident (active duty stationed in Maryland counts) and enrolled at least half time. Apply through the MHEC One-App on the MDCAPS portal and upload your DD-214 or orders showing the deployment (plus a marriage or birth certificate for family members). The 2025-2026 window ran April 15, 2025 to April 1, 2026; renewals get first priority, then veterans, then dependents. Awards last up to 4 years full time or 8 years part time.
benefits.source_title: Maryland Higher Education Commission - Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Program

benefits.benefit: In-state tuition at Maryland public colleges for honorably discharged veterans, service members, and families
benefits.details: Education Article 15-106.4 exempts you from nonresident tuition at any Maryland public college or university if you are an honorably discharged veteran who 'resides in this State' or 'is domiciled in this State.' There is no waiting period and no disability rating requirement. Active service members stationed in, living in, or domiciled in Maryland and their spouses and financially dependent children also pay in-state rates, and the family keeps the rate while continuously enrolled even if the member moves. Public schools must also follow federal in-state tuition rules for GI Bill users. Show your DD-214 and proof of Maryland residence to the school's registrar or veterans office.
benefits.source_title: Maryland General Assembly - Education Article 15-106.4 (Exemption from nonresident tuition for service members, veterans, and dependents)

benefits.benefit: Military retirement income subtraction ($12,500 under age 55; $20,000 age 55 and older)
benefits.details: Maryland taxes military retired pay, but Tax-General 10-207(q) lets you subtract 'the first $12,500 of military retirement income' if you are under 55 on the last day of the tax year, and 'the first $20,000' if you are 55 or older. 'Military retirement income' means 'retirement income, including death benefits, received as a result of military service,' so Survivor Benefit Plan payments to a surviving spouse count. Claim it on Form 502 (see Instruction 13). A 2026 bill (HB 857) to raise the under-55 amount to $20,000 did not pass. VA disability compensation is not part of federal adjusted gross income, which is where Maryland starts, so it is not taxed. Retirees 65 or older or totally disabled may instead qualify for the general Maryland pension exclusion.
benefits.source_title: Maryland General Assembly - Tax-General Article 10-207(q) (Subtraction for military retirement income); DVMF Retirement Pay and Pension Tax Deductions page (updated Jan. 16, 2026)

benefits.benefit: 10-point veterans credit on state job selection tests (spouses and surviving spouses included)
benefits.details: For state government jobs filled by a selection test, the appointing authority 'shall apply a credit of 10 points' to the passing score of an 'eligible veteran' (honorable discharge or certificate of satisfactory completion of service, including reserves), 'the spouse of an eligible veteran who has a service connected disability,' the 'surviving spouse of a deceased eligible veteran,' and the spouse of an active service member. Former prisoners of war get 2 more points. Current state employees and veterans convicted of a crime after discharge are not eligible. Maryland law no longer gives extra points for the veteran's own service-connected disability; a separate 5-point credit applies to any applicant with a disability under the ADA. Claim the credit on your state application through the Department of Budget and Management and have your DD-214 ready.

benefits.benefit: Charlotte Hall Veterans Home (state assisted living and nursing home)
benefits.details: Maryland's only state veterans home is at 29449 Charlotte Hall Road in St. Mary's County. You must be a Maryland resident veteran who served on full-time active duty (not just training) with a discharge other than dishonorable, and be at least 62 or found disabled by Social Security or the VA. Certain reserve members and certain non-veteran spouses can also be admitted (spouses pay the full assisted living cost). Cost depends on income and your VA rating; every veteran gets a VA per diem credit, and a veteran 'rated 70% or greater for a service-connected disability may be entitled to the full cost of nursing home care.' Assisted living residents generally pay 90% of net monthly income. Start by calling the Veterans Service Officer at 301-884-8171 ext. 5112, then mail or email the admission application to the home. The home may decline an applicant for health, safety, or welfare reasons.
benefits.source_title: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families - Charlotte Hall Veterans Home

benefits.benefit: Burial in one of five Maryland State Veterans Cemeteries at no cost to the veteran
benefits.details: Eligible veterans receive a plot, grave liner, headstone, and interment services 'at no expense' at Cheltenham (Prince George's County), Crownsville (Anne Arundel), Garrison Forest in Owings Mills (Baltimore County), Rocky Gap in Flintstone (Allegany), or Eastern Shore in Hurlock (Dorchester). Eligibility follows the VA National Cemetery Administration rules; any discharge other than dishonorable qualifies. National Guard members and reservists must also show at least 2 years of Maryland residency. Spouses, minor children, and some unmarried adult dependent children can be buried too; the fee for dependents, Guard members, and reservists is $1,002 (adjusted each October 1). You can pre-register by mailing the Pre-Application Interment Planning form to the cemetery, but the final decision is made at the time of death. The family or funeral director calls the cemetery to schedule and provides the DD-214.

benefits.benefit: Maryland Veterans Trust Fund emergency grants (rent, mortgage, utilities, car, repairs)
benefits.details: The Trust Fund makes one-time grants, paid straight to the landlord, lender, utility, or repair shop, for Maryland residents who are honorably discharged veterans, Maryland National Guard members, or their surviving spouses and who face a financial hardship. Covered items are past-due rent or mortgage, past-due utilities, past-due car and insurance payments, and reimbursement of emergency car or home repairs. Bills must be 30 to 60 days past due when you apply. Apply online through the Trust Fund portal with your DD-214, proof of Maryland residency, proof of income, bank statements, the past-due notices, your lease or mortgage statement, vendor payment details, and a short written plan. Applications are taken the 1st through 15th of each month, reviewed the 16th through 23rd, and decided by month end. Awards depend on available funding; no maximum amount is published. The agency also funds a Service Animal Program through grants to nonprofit groups, not direct payments to veterans.
